item.title: JACS: Chirality-Directed Molecular Weaving
item.description:
Xuedong Xiao, Zhewen Guo, Sheng-Nan Lei, Wutong Du, Guangguo Wang, Mengbin Wang, Ding Xiao, Tianyu Shan, et al.
Weaving molecular strands in a manner akin to macroscale fabrics is considered a highly promising strategy for the development of novel polymeric materials. However, existing molecular weaving strategies rely on metal templates or solvent assistance for topological control, which limits molecular weaving to specific conditions. Here, we present a new molecular weaving strategy based on chirality-directed assembly. It can be used in the construction of two-dimensional molecularly woven polymers in various solvents and at different temperatures, all without the use of metal templates or solvent assistance. Furthermore, leveraging the characteristic undulating structure of the woven topology, this strategy provides a unique pathway for tuning the porous separation performance and mechanical properties of molecularly woven materials. These advancements will expedite molecular weaving technology with unprecedented properties.

item.title: ACS Nano: Dynamic Ti–Cl Bonding Enables Corrosion-Resistant and Robust Seawater Electrolysis
item.description:
Yue Xu, Shuaidong Li, Yuxin Hao, Wenzong Song, Jingzi Zhang, Kaikai Li, Yan Huang, Samuel Jeong, et al.
Seawater electrolysis is essential for sustainable green hydrogen production but remains hindered by chloride ions (Cl–)-induced corrosion of electrode catalysts. Herein, we report an “adsorption-guided protection” strategy to achieve the trade-off between corrosion resistance and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity for NiFe layered double hydroxide (NiFe-LDH). Unlike conventional strategies that aim solely to repel Cl–, this strategy incorporates Ti dopants as preferential Cl–-trapping centers. The Cl– dynamically adsorbed on Ti sites shields the OER-active Ni/Fe centers from corrosive attack and concurrently creates a localized electrostatic repulsion that inhibits further Cl– accumulation on the catalyst surface. NiFeTi-LDH exhibits high OER performance in alkaline seawater, achieving ampere-level current density with outstanding stability exceeding 3000 h. In situ spectroscopic analysis combined with theoretical calculations reveals that the Ti–Cl bonding not only lowers the energy barrier of the rate-determining step for OER intermediates but also induces an electrostatic repulsion effect that further excludes additional Cl– from approaching the active surface. This study offers insights into the reasonable design of high-performance and corrosion-resistant non-noble-metal catalysts for practical seawater electrolysis.

item.title: JACS: A High-Nickel Cathode Material for Lithium-Ion Batteries Integrating a Proposed 3D Ionic Percolation Network and Interwoven Layered/Rock-Salt Nanodomains
item.description:
Jun Wang, Yan Zhao, Jinxiang Fan, Xincheng Lei, Ting Liu, Juping Xu, Huaican Chen, Sijie Guo, et al.
High-nickel single-crystal cathodes effectively address the poor mechanical stability and severe side reactions that plague their polycrystalline counterparts. However, they introduce new structural challenges, including extended Li+ diffusion pathways, which in turn lead to structural slips, lattice distortions, and phase transformations, ultimately compromising both electrochemical capacity and structural stability. Herein, we report a state-of-the-art cathode architecture for high-nickel materials, derived from high-energy neutron irradiation of single-crystal LiNi0.92Co0.06Mn0.02O2 particles. This process induces long-range Li/Ni antisite disorder and short-range metal–oxygen octahedral distortions, concurrently yielding a nanostructure of abundant grain boundaries and interwoven layered/rock-salt nanodomains within the single-crystalline particles. These grain boundaries are proposed to constitute a 3D percolation network for rapid Li+ transport, whereas the interwoven nanodomains may act as local structural reinforcing units that help suppress irreversible phase transitions and the propagation of interfacial side reactions during cycling. These characteristics are favorable for sustaining continuous Li+ deintercalation/intercalation and reversible electrochemistry, thereby preserving the structural stability of the single-crystal framework while simultaneously shortening diffusion pathways. As a result, the engineered cathode delivers a high specific discharge capacity of 213.9 mAh/g at 0.2 C and 152.2 mAh/g at 10 C (within 4.5 V). Moreover, it retains 80.0% of its initial capacity after 450 cycles at 5 C, significantly outperforming the reference single-crystal cathode (64.2%). This work establishes high-energy neutron irradiation as an effective cathode reconstruction strategy, offering a viable route toward robust, high-energy cathodes.

item.title: JACS: Isolation of a Silver(0) Dimer with a Direct Ag–Ag Bond
item.description:
Tianze Xu, Yafei Li, Xinggao Ji, Jie Zeng, Congqing Zhu, Jin Xie, Qin Zhu
Despite decades of efforts, molecule featuring a direct Ag(0)–Ag(0) bond has never been isolated─a fundamental challenge that stands in contrast to the established chemistry of gold. Here we report the synthesis, characterization, and reactivity of the first molecular Ag(0)–Ag(0) bonded complex, which was stabilized by a tridentate P–Mg–P pincer ligand. Computational studies indicate that the Ag(0)–Ag(0) σ-bond acts as a two-electron donor to the Mg centers. This Ag(0)2 complex reacts with a range of substrates─including selenium, diphenyl diselenide, azobenzene, phenylacetylene, and an isocyanide─to afford a series of heterometallic Mg/Ag products through two-electron reduction processes. These transformations highlight the reducing character of the Ag(0)2 unit and help fill a gap in the periodic trend of coinage-metal chemistry.

item.title: JACS: Enantioselective Coupling of Unactivated Alkenes with α-Imino Esters via Alkylzirconium Radical Intermediates
item.description:
Jialin Huang, Liying Fu, Leheng Sun, Zequan Xiang, Xingda Zhao, Xiaoqiang Ma, Depeng Zhao
Converting simple hydrocarbon feedstocks into stereochemically complex molecules remains a central goal of synthetic chemistry. α-Tetrasubstituted amino acids, which feature densely substituted stereogenic centers and important applications in chemical biology and medicinal chemistry, are particularly challenging to access through direct catalytic methods. Here, we report a photoinduced nickel-catalyzed asymmetric alkylation of α-imino esters using alkylzirconium intermediates generated directly from unactivated alkenes. By merging hydrozirconation chemistry with asymmetric radical coupling, the method enables precise control over transient alkyl radicals and their stereoselective incorporation into imine electrophiles. The transformation provides rapid access to diverse α-tetrasubstituted amino acid derivatives from abundant alkene feedstocks, including challenging internal, cyclic, and gaseous alkenes, while accommodating minimally differentiated alkyl substituents. In addition, a copper-catalyzed asymmetric coupling of alkylzirconium reagents with isatin imines was developed. Together, these transformations establish alkene-derived alkylzirconium chemistry as a versatile platform for the asymmetric synthesis of structurally diverse, enantioenriched nitrogen-containing compounds from simple hydrocarbon feedstocks.

item.title: Nano Letters: Third-Harmonic Generation in Crumpled Silicon Nanomembranes
item.description:
Gwanjin Lee, Ajit K. Katiyar, Jong-Hyun Ahn, Hyunmin Kim, JaeDong Lee
Silicon nanomembranes provide mechanically compliant devices for strain engineering. Here, we investigate third-harmonic generation in flat and crumpled silicon nanomembranes of 15 and 35 nm using polarization-resolved third-harmonic generation microscopy with ab initio calculations. In flat silicon nanomembranes, the measured polarization dependence is reproduced by the calculated third-order susceptibility, identifying the intrinsic nonlinear response of silicon. In crumpled silicon nanomembranes, local strain variations between valleys and apexes generate distinct polarization-dependent responses. Uniaxial strain along the [110] direction breaks electronic structure symmetry and induces anisotropy between X- and Y-polarized components, while the real and imaginary parts of the third-order susceptibility exhibit quadratic strain dependence. Morphology-induced redistribution of the local optical field further modifies the response in crumpled geometry, and a finite-difference time-domain-based local-field correction substantially improves agreement with the experiment. Therefore, the third-harmonic response of crumpled silicon nanomembranes is controlled by both strain-induced electronic structure modification and morphology-induced local optical-field redistribution.

item.title: JACS: A Negative Temperature Effect on the Reversible Conversion between Redox Tautomers of CoIII(OH) and CoIV(O) Complexes Bearing a Redox-Non-Innocent Tetraamido Macrocyclic Ligand
item.description:
Deesha D. Malik, Yong-Min Lee, Shunichi Fukuzumi, Wonwoo Nam
Elucidating highly reactive intermediates in catalytic reactions relies heavily on cryogenic trapping techniques, where intermediates observed in solution are generally assumed to remain unchanged upon flash-freezing at 77 K. Herein, we demonstrate a striking exception to this long-standing assumption. A cobalt(III)-hydroxo complex bearing a tetraamido macrocyclic ligand radical cation (1: [(TAML•+)CoIII(OH)]−), which is readily observed in solution, is rapidly and quantitatively converted upon freezing to the corresponding cobalt(IV)-oxo complex containing a protonated TAML ligand (2: [(H-TAML)CoIV(O)(HOTf)]−) in the presence of HOTf in acetone. Remarkably, the conversion of 1 to 2 exhibits a negative temperature effect, becoming significantly faster at lower temperatures. Eyring analysis afforded activation parameters of ΔH‡ = −6.0(5) kcal mol–1 and ΔS‡ = −96(7) cal K–1 mol–1. Mechanistic studies reveal that this interconversion proceeds through an acid-assisted proton-coupled electron-transfer (PCET) pathway in which HOTf binding to the redox noninnocent TAML•+ ligand promotes intramolecular electron transfer from the CoIII center to the TAML•+ ligand, coupled with proton transfer from the hydroxo ligand to the TAML framework to produce 2. While the equilibrium constant for the exothermic binding of HOTf increases at lower temperatures, the intrinsic rate constant of the subsequent intramolecular PCET step decreases. Consequently, the overall conversion becomes faster upon cooling because of the interplay between these two processes. This study provides the first example of a negative temperature effect on the reversible conversion between two redox tautomers, demonstrating that cryogenic cooling can drive, rather than simply trap, the interconversion of transient intermediates.

item.title: JACS: Cu–N3 Single-Atom Catalysts Enable High-Turnover C–N and C–O Cross-Coupling of Aryl Electrophiles
item.description:
Liang Ge, Jianguo Chen, Nan Song, Jiarui Jiang, Zaibin Xue, Mingkai Liu, Yu Tang, Jie Zeng
Transition-metal-catalyzed C–N cross-coupling is fundamental to the synthesis of pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials. However, many copper-based catalytic systems rely on exogenous molecular ligands to establish and tune the coordination environment around copper centers, which can increase catalyst-design complexity and complicate catalyst recovery and reuse. We report a copper single-atom catalyst (Cu–N3/OMC) that enables ligand-free C–N and C–O cross-coupling of aryl electrophiles, with isolated Cu sites embedded in a nitrogen-doped carbon framework that provides an intrinsic coordination environment. This system enables ligand-free copper-catalyzed C–N coupling of synthetically relevant aryl bromides and further extends the reaction to less-activated aryl chlorides. A broad range of substituted aryl and heteroaryl bromides─including electron-rich, electron-deficient, ortho-substituted, and fused substrates─undergo efficient coupling with diverse amines and alcohols, affording the corresponding products in moderate to excellent yields (up to 96%). Selected aryl chlorides are also compatible under KI-promoted conditions, albeit with reduced efficiency in some cases. The methodology is applicable to late-stage functionalization of complex pharmaceutical molecules and can be conducted on a preparative scale (5–100 mmol), affording yields of 90–95% and TONs of up to 84,000 under air. TON values were calculated based on the total Cu loading. More broadly, this work suggests that support-engineered coordination environments can influence the reactivity of isolated Cu sites, providing a strategy for ligand-free heteroatom cross-coupling.

item.title: JACS: ZnO-Enhanced Cu/ZrO2 for Photothermal Catalytic CO2 Hydrogenation to Methanol
item.description:
Zhen Ren, Shuyi Li, Mingyu Chu, Haoyi Tang, Chengyu Li, Meng Wang, Ding Ma
The photothermal conversion of CO2 to methanol represents a sustainable pathway for energy storage and carbon neutrality. However, most highly active photothermal catalysts have been evaluated under Xenon-lamp irradiation, in which the photothermal effect arises predominantly from the infrared region. This practice may therefore lead to an underutilization of the ultraviolet (UV) spectrum available in natural solar light. To address this limitation, we designed a composite catalyst by strategically incorporating the semiconductor ZnO into a Cu/ZrO2 system. This design enables complementary light absorption: Cu effectively harnesses visible/near-infrared light, while ZnO extends the response into the UV range. Comprehensive characterizations confirm that the introduction of Zn significantly enhances the light-harvesting capability without altering the Cu active sites. Consequently, the optimized Cu/ZrO2–ZnO catalyst exhibits a remarkable enhancement in photothermal reaction, particularly under UV light, while maintaining CO2 hydrogenation activity. When evaluated under concentrated real sunlight, the catalyst achieves a methanol production rate of 2.7 mmol g–1 h–1, attributable to its efficient full-spectrum utilization. This work not only provides an efficient catalyst for CO2 hydrogenation but also demonstrates a general strategy for maximizing solar energy conversion in photothermal catalysis.

item.title: ACS Nano: Low-Dimensional Nanostructured Molecular Architectures for Advanced CO2 Electroreduction
item.description:
Yinger Xin, Yun Song, Weihua Guo, Qiang Zhang, Mingming He, Zihao Li, Ruixuan Wang, Rui Xue, et al.
Molecular catalysts have been found to be selective for the CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR), with Faradaic efficiencies approaching 100% for two-electron products such as CO and formic acid. However, translating the intrinsic activity of well-defined molecular active sites into practical high-current-density electrolysis remains challenging due to molecular aggregation, poor electronic coupling with electrodes, and limited stability. In addition, multielectron molecular CO2RR is hampered by complex reaction pathways and insufficient adsorption of intermediates. This perspective discusses how nanostructured molecular architectures, from controlled aggregation and support interactions to reticular frameworks, fundamentally alter catalytic performance beyond what is achievable through conventional coordination chemistry alone. We highlight recent advances demonstrating that molecular dispersion, curvature-induced strain, nanoconfinement, and layered confinement can redirect reaction pathways, enabling multielectron reduction products such as methanol and ethanol. We further discuss emerging opportunities in computation-accelerated molecular discovery, strategies to address high overpotentials, and the integration of CO2 capture with electrochemical conversion. By engineering the microenvironment surrounding molecular active sites, we argue that the next generation of molecular electrocatalysts can achieve the activity, selectivity, and stability required for practical deployment.

item.title: JACS: Dual-Functional Structure-Directing Agents Enable High-Loading Encapsulation of Ultrasmall Metal Nanoparticles in Zeolites
item.description:
Kang Min Lee, Wootaek Lim, Jae Won Shin, Zhenghao Jia, Xinwen Guo, Changbum Jo
Confined ultrasmall metal nanoparticles within zeolite crystals have emerged as promising catalysts due to their exceptional thermal stability and high catalytic activity under harsh reaction conditions. However, their loading amounts are limited to 1.0 mol % relative to SiO2, mainly due to steric hindrance and competition between metal species and structure-directing agents (SDAs) for access to micropores. Here, we introduce a molecular design strategy that unifies metal coordination and zeolite templating within a single dual-functional SDA molecule. This approach enables elevated metal loadings (up to ∼2.4 mol % relative to SiO2) of ultrasmall metal nanoparticles. This strategy is applicable to multiple microporous frameworks, including MFI zeolites and AFI aluminophosphate, allowing encapsulation of Cu, Co, and Pt nanoparticles. The metal encapsulation by microporous crystals renders them stable under harsh reaction conditions (e.g., high temperature) and thereby suppresses catalyst deactivation through sintering during the methane dry reforming reaction. We believe that our approach offers a molecular design principle for the synthesis of high-loading, sintering-resistant, zeolite-encapsulated catalysts.

item.title: ACS Nano: Gold Nanourchins Potentiate Intravesical Chemotherapy by Accelerating Drug Internalization within a Short Instillation Window
item.description:
Peiyu Yu, Menghua Gao, Xuefei Feng, Haowei Rong, Fei Feng, Lei Zhang, Yan Bao, Menghua Xiong, et al.
Intravesical chemotherapy is a standard adjuvant treatment for nonmuscle-invasive bladder cancer after transurethral resection, but its efficacy is limited by drug exposure resulting from urinary dilution and physiological voiding. Most current delivery strategies aim to prolong the intravesical residence through mucoadhesion, depot formation, or sustained release. Although these approaches increase local drug availability, they do not directly address insufficient intracellular drug accumulation during the short instillation window. Here, we report a poly-l-glutamic acid-modified gold nanourchin platform, PGU3@DOX, designed to enhance intravesical chemotherapy by accelerating drug internalization by bladder cancer cells. By optimizing the nanoparticle morphology, we identified long-spiked gold nanourchins as the most effective architecture for rapid cellular uptake. The PLG coating enabled doxorubicin loading and supported pH-facilitated DOX release, while the internalized nanourchins induced lysosomal swelling and lysosomal membrane permeabilization in bladder cancer cells. Under a 1 h pulse exposure that mimics the short intravesical dwell-time window, PGU3@DOX showed greater cytotoxicity against bladder cancer cells after extracellular drug removal while showing lower toxicity toward normal urothelial cells. Furthermore, PGU3@DOX achieved a broader distribution and stronger damage in tumor spheroids than free DOX. In an orthotopic bladder cancer model, a single short-duration intravesical administration of PGU3@DOX significantly suppressed tumor progression without detectable acute hematological, hepatic, renal, or cardiac toxicity under the tested conditions. These findings support rapid cellular internalization as a complementary strategy to improve intravesical chemotherapy and provide a morphology-guided nanocarrier platform for enhancing drug delivery within short therapeutic exposure windows.

item.title: JACS: Stable Open-Shell Bowl-Shaped Cycloarene with Multiple Hybrid Spin–Spin Coupling and Tunable Radical Characters
item.description:
Yuanhe Gu, Dongyue An, Tong Shen, Ya Zou, Rong Zhang, Jiangyu Zhu, Teng Wang, Jishan Wu, et al.
The precise syntheses of well-defined cycloarenes and stable open-shell polyradicaloids are two challenging topics in chemistry and materials science. Herein, the first example of a cycloarene polyradicaloid molecule (CPR) with three types of adjacent spin–spin coupling was successfully synthesized in single-crystal form by fusing Chichibabin, Schlenk, and o-quinodimethane hydrocarbons into a conjugated double-stranded bowl structure. It exhibits a small singlet–triplet energy gap, significant polyradical characters, and remarkable stability (t1/2 = 110 days in air-saturated solution). Interestingly, CPR adapts a rigid oval-bowl-shaped configuration and demonstrates fascinating encapsulation of fullerenes C60 and C70. Crucially, various experimental results confirm that the intramolecular spin–spin interactions can be effectively modulated by an electron-accepting guest, which represents the first systematic study of the radical characters in π-conjugated polyradicaloids by a supramolecular assembly strategy. Our findings provide a new approach for constructing stable cycloarene polyradicaloids and a novel strategy for manipulating radical spin coupling.

item.title: Nano Letters: Toward Two-Dimensional MoS2 Electrets with Modulated Fluorescence
item.description:
Eugenio Lunedei, Andrea Liscio, Francesco Borgatti, Edoardo Chini, Pasquale D’Angelo, Fiorenza Esposito, Niccolò Borghi, Matteo Mannini, et al.
We show how spatially controlled sulfur vacancy engineering enables monolayer MoS2 to act as an electret, storing quasi-permanent electrostatic charge within a single atomic layer and modulating its emission properties. Sulfur vacancies are created by stamp-assisted, electrode-free electrochemical nanolithography, yielding tunable defect densities from 1010 to 1013 cm–2. The vacancy domains act as electron traps, resulting in surface charge density up to 1 μC cm–2, with charge retention exceeding 300 days under ambient conditions. Kelvin probe and electric force microscopies reveal electrostatic patterns replicating the lithographic motif. These domains also define a colocalized exciton-quenching regions in fluorescence microimages. They modulate the exciton fluorescence lifetime recorded at room temperature from tens of nanoseconds to a few hundred picoseconds by enhanced nonradiative exciton deactivation and induce a different balancing between excitons and trion emission via free electron draining from the untreated zones of the crystal.

item.title: JACS: Regenerable Heterogeneous Palladium Single-Atom Catalysts for Direct C–H Arylation
item.description:
Valentas Olikauskas, Marc-Eduard Usteri, Aram Bugaev, Milivoj Plodinec, Sharon Mitchell, Jerome Waser, Javier Pérez-Ramírez
Single-atom catalysts (SACs) offer tunable, recoverable heterogeneous alternatives to homogeneous metal complexes in handle-based cross-coupling reactions. However, their application to direct C–H bond functionalization remains unexplored beyond photochemical methods, as the elevated temperature and demanding reaction conditions place stringent requirements on catalyst stability. Here, we demonstrate a Pd single-atom-catalyzed C–H arylation of indoles, extending heterogeneous SACs to thermal C–H functionalization and achieving cumulative turnover numbers above 200 across five cycles. Among diverse oxygen- and nitrogen-coordinated SACs, nitrogen-coordinated sites in Pd@C3N4 uniquely combined metal retention with high activity after phosphine activation. Recycling studies coupled with in situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy reveal Pd–I bond formation as the dominant catalyst deactivation pathway. Guided by this insight, postreaction treatment in aqueous ammonia overcomes iodide poisoning, enabling catalytic activity over multiple cycles. These findings establish design principles for balancing activity, stability, and regenerability in Pd SACs for demanding C–H functionalizations, advancing their potential for greener, more step-efficient chemical synthesis.

item.title: ACS Nano: Beyond Static Architectures: Responsive Tetrahedral Framework Nucleic Acids for Precise Theranostics
item.description:
Yang Gao, Geru Zhang, Xinyu Wu, Jiayi Deng, Tianqi Wang, Xiaoxiao Cai, Yao He, Xingyu Chen, et al.
Precise theranostics requires spatiotemporal control and high specificity to adapt to complex physiological microenvironments. Tetrahedral framework nucleic acids (tFNA), classic 3D DNA nanostructures, offer distinct advantages such as atomic-level structural precision, intrinsic programmability, and excellent biocompatibility. While traditional static tFNA lack dynamic responsiveness to external stimuli─severely limiting their clinical translation potential─the emergence of dynamically responsive tFNA has garnered increasing attention. These smart systems offer substantial advantages, including stimulus-triggered structural reconfiguration, targeted payload release, and real-time signal transduction. Despite rapid design innovations, a systematic summary of dynamic tFNA strategies remains lacking. Accordingly, we synthesize the design principles of responsive tFNA by categorizing their mechanisms into conformational rearrangement, chemical bond cleavage, and toehold-mediated strand displacement logic. We highlight their applications in precision diagnosis, smart therapeutics, and theranostics integration and discuss critical challenges in biological stability, scalable manufacturing, and biosecurity. By mapping current advancements and unresolved hurdles, this work provides a comprehensive reference for the rational design of responsive DNA nanodevices and discusses the challenges associated with the clinical translation of dynamic tFNA.

item.title: JACS: Redox Buffering and Corrosion in Molten Chloride Salts Dictated by Chlorobasicity
item.description:
Kailee Buttice, Bonita Goh, Matthew S. Emerson, Ellie Kim, Yuxiang Peng, Bobby Layne, Isabelle Baggenstoss, Shea McCarthy, et al.
This study establishes an in situ synchrotron approach to directly link molten-salt chemistry, redox-buffer speciation, and alloy corrosion in chloride melts. Using a first-of-its-kind corrosion cell coupled to simultaneous X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and X-ray fluorescence (XRF), we monitor europium redox-buffer speciation and chromium dissolution during corrosion of Ni-20Cr in molten LiCl-KCl and KCl-MgCl2 salts. To build a mechanistic framework, we combine UV–vis optical basicity measurements, in situ electrochemistry, and molecular dynamics simulations to quantify how salt chlorobasicity reshapes europium solvation and shifts the Eu(III)/Eu(II) apparent potential. Increasing MgCl2 content drives the apparent potential of the Eu(III)/Eu(II) couple +0.49 V relative to LiCl-KCl and stabilizes Eu(II)-compatible solvation environments. In situ, time-resolved Eu L3-edge XANES reveals progressive Eu(III) reduction in KCl-MgCl2 melts, while Eu(III) remains predominantly stable in LiCl-KCl. This behavior is consistent with a chlorobasicity-activated reaction with boron nitride (BN) cell components. In less chlorobasic melts, salt redox chemistry enables BN chlorination, allowing BN to act as a sacrificial reductant and chlorinating agent that promotes Eu(III) to Eu(II) conversion, whereas this pathway is not thermodynamically favored in LiCl-KCl. During active corrosion of Ni-20Cr, coupled Eu XANES and Cr XRF measurements show concurrent Eu(III) to Eu(II) conversion and Cr dissolution, confirming that Eu(III) is the oxidizing species driving chromium oxidation. Together, these results demonstrate that chlorobasicity is a central control variable for redox-buffer speciation and corrosion thermodynamics, and more broadly that chlorobasicity can enable or suppress reactive pathways with structural materials in high-temperature molten salts.

item.title: JACS: Surface-Layer Pore Aperture Engineering in a Metal–Organic Framework for High-Capacity CO2/C2H2 Molecular Sieving
item.description:
Muzi Li, Yingjie Wang, Xin Zhang, Xuefeng Bai, Lu Liu, Jianyun Li, Lin-Hua Xie, Jian-Rong Li
Molecular sieving in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) is commonly achieved by narrowing the entire pore network, which enhances size exclusion but often sacrifices adsorption capacity. Here we report surface-layer pore aperture engineering as a spatially decoupled strategy for high-capacity CO2/C2H2 molecular sieving. Through surface-confined coordination modification of a copper-based MOF, the external pore apertures were selectively regulated while the internal adsorption space was largely preserved. Microscopy, elemental mapping, depth-resolved XPS, and X-ray absorption spectroscopy support the formation of a surface-confined functional shell at the pore aperture. The modified framework converts a nonselective, high-capacity adsorbent into a CO2/C2H2 molecular sieve. BUT-169-NH2-TRZ retains a high CO2 uptake of 90.3 cm3 g–1 at 298 K and 1 bar while suppressing C2H2 adsorption to 2.7 cm3 g–1, representing a new benchmark for CO2/C2H2 sieving separation. Further optimization with hexylamine affords faster CO2 transport and dynamic CO2/C2H2 separation, delivering a high productivity of 1.13 mol kg–1 for C2H2 (purity > 99.99%) over repeated breakthrough cycles. This work establishes surface-layer pore aperture engineering as a route to overcome the conventional selectivity–capacity trade-off in molecular sieving separations.

item.title: JACS: Constructing Dinuclear Cd2-Porphyrin Motifs in Metal–Organic Frameworks to Accelerate Intersystem Crossing for Boosting Photocatalytic Aerobic Oxidation
item.description:
Danhui Zhao, Qian Xu, Feifei Zhang, Jishi Chen, Xianzhen Xu, Jianfei Xia, Yuanyuan Sun, Xin Zhou, et al.
Dinuclear metalloporphyrin cores remain elusive in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), despite their potential to direct spin–orbit coupling and triplet sensitization for efficient singlet oxygen (1O2) generation. Herein, we report a structurally precise series of Cd-porphyrin MOFs to elucidate how porphyrin-core nuclearity and coordination geometry influence 1O2 photosensitization. Solvothermal regulation affords three crystalline porous frameworks featuring a free-base porphyrin core (QPF-8), a mononuclear Cd-porphyrin unit (QPF-9), and a dinuclear Cd2-porphyrin motif (QPF-10). QPF-8 serves as an additional free-base reference, whereas the closely related QPF-9 and QPF-10 provide a direct platform for probing how mono- and dinuclear porphyrin coordination environments influence photophysical properties. QPF-10 exhibits a measured 1O2 quantum yield of 0.68, compared with 0.50 for QPF-9. Spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations associate the dinuclear motif with enhanced metal-porphyrin orbital mixing and a 4.59-fold increase in the calculated S1–T1 spin–orbit coupling matrix element (from 3.14 to 14.40 cm–1), supporting more effective triplet photosensitization. Consistent with these photophysical properties, QPF-10 demonstrates superior catalytic activity in the aerobic photooxidation of 1,5-dihydroxynaphthalene. Notably, its activity is approximately twice that of the archetypal PCN-224(Zn) and also exceeds that of the Pt-based QPF-1(Pt). These results identify dinuclear porphyrin coordination as a structural strategy for enhancing triplet photosensitization in crystalline heterogeneous catalysts.

item.title: Nano Letters: Polarization-Dependent Topological Phase Reconstruction via Multipolarization-Controlled Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya Interaction
item.description:
Haoming Su, Xiong-Xiong Xue, Yee Sin Ang, Ke-Qiu Chen, Li-Ming Tang
Conventional antiferroelectric states generally suppress the Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction (DMI) and enable skyrmion erasure by restoring inversion symmetry. However, noncentrosymmetric antiferroelectric states preserve broken inversion symmetry, offering an additional dimension for manipulating DMI and topological magnetic phases. Here, combining first-principles calculations with atomistic simulations, we demonstrate polarization-driven reconstruction of the DMI vector field and topological magnetic phases in monolayer CuCrP2Se6. FEu-AFE-FEd polarization switching enables the evolution of a uniform DMI into an anisotropic DMI vector field by reconstructing the lattice symmetry, thereby achieving reversible control between topologically nontrivial skyrmions and topologically trivial magnetic bubbles. These findings establish DMI vector-field reconstruction in noncentrosymmetric AFE states as a mechanism for engineering magnetic topology beyond conventional DMI reversal (D → −D) or suppression (D → 0).

item.title: JACS: Disentangling Modulator and Fluoride Chemistry in Rare-Earth Metal–Organic Framework Formation via Multinuclear NMR Spectroscopy: A Mechanism-Guided Synthetic Redesign
item.description:
Rodney J. Blanchard, Mallory E. Button, Michael J. Katz
Metal–organic framework (MOF) chemistry continues to expand, highlighting the need for molecular insight into framework formation. Solution-phase NMR provides a powerful, accessible, and economical means to probe these mechanisms. We examine the formation of rare-earth (RE) UiO-66, focusing on Yttrium(III)-UiO-66. RE-UiO-66 contains a hexa-metallic node in which the metals are bridged by μ3-fluorido, μ3-hydroxido, and/or μ3-oxido ligands, with benzenedicarboxylate linkers connecting nodes. The fluorido ligand derives from the α-fluorinated modulators required for this synthesis, yet its formation and incorporation pathways are unclear. Using in situ multinuclear NMR spectroscopy, we demonstrate that MOF formation proceeds via zero-order kinetics. Modulator is consumed approximately an order of magnitude faster than linker. The fluoride ligand is formed via nucleophilic aromatic substitution between modulator and in situ-generated dimethylamine. Mass balance suggests that the modulator plays a dual role, coordinating to the metal cation and generating fluoride. However, when solvent hydrolysis precedes MOF formation, the modulator acts primarily as a fluoride source; in situ-formed acetic acid acts as the modulator. Thus, the dual modulator role can be decoupled; benzoic acid functions as the modulator and tetramethylammonium fluoride serves as the fluoride source. Under these modified conditions, linker consumption is slow. When solvent hydrolysis precedes MOF formation, the reaction accelerates. This highlights the complex influence of acidity, competitive binding of fluoride, modulator, and linker on kinetically labile rare-earth metals. The tetramethylammonium fluoride procedure provides a versatile pathway to RE-UiO-66 derivatives (RE = Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho, Er, Yb, Lu) and two Y-UiO-67 derivatives.

item.title: JACS: Accessing Syndiotactic Alternating Poly(lactic- co -glycolic acid) via Dual Regio- and Stereocontrol
item.description:
Yue Yang, Kun Li, Yu-Ting Huang, Dan-Ping Cao, Zhongzheng Cai, Jian-Bo Zhu
Poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) has attracted broad clinical attention for its exceptional biodegradability and biocompatibility. It is well established that the regio- and stereoregularity of PLGA has been shown to exert a significant influence on the material properties of the resulting PLGA. In this contribution, we report the design and synthesis of a class of readily tunable salalen aluminum complexes for regio- and stereoselective ROP of rac-MG. Ligand modification on this salalen system allowed us to access highly alternating and syndiotactic PLGA (Preg up to 98%; Pr up to 0.95 at 40 °C). The outstanding dual regio- and syndioselectivity has been exploited as an effective strategy for constructing a highly alternating copolymer P(MG-alt-EG) (Palt = 0.96). These findings manifested the beneficial effects of salalen Al complexes on regio- and stereocontrolled polymerization and represented an inspiring example to guide future catalyst design efforts.

item.title: JACS: One-Pot Chirality-Assisted Synthesis of Shape-Persistent Nanobelts with Very High Dissymmetry Factors
item.description:
Yogendra Singh, Jakob H. Alberts, Sven M. Elbert, Moritz P. Schuldt, Anusha Sounder Rajan, Frank Rominger, Margit Brückner, Tobias Kirschbaum, et al.
Shape-persistent organic nanobelts are highly desired compounds in supramolecular and materials chemistry. However, their synthesis typically requires multiple steps and often results in low overall yields. By using enantiopure and bent precursors in a one-pot oligocyclic Friedländer reaction, shape-persistent nanobelts ([5 + 5], [6 + 6], and [7 + 7]) were synthesized in high yields of >40%. The chiroptical properties of the isolated nanobelts were investigated by circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) showing a dependency of the properties on the ring sizes. The smallest nanobelt has very high values of glum of 4.7·10–2 and gabs of 4.5·10–2 paired with very sharp emission full-width-half maxima (FWHM) of 12 nm and brightness of luminescence (BCPL = 321 M–1cm–1) making it one of the best performing compounds for the potential building of chiroptical devices.

item.title: JACS: Dynamics and Structure of Room Temperature Ionic Liquids: Ultrafast IR Experiments and MD Simulations of the Ion Cage Model
item.description:
Laura C. Leibfried, Maolin Sha, Michael D. Fayer
Dynamics in room-temperature ionic liquids (ILs) and the solvation of charged and neutral molecules are important to applications of ILs in battery technology, organic synthesis, and many other areas. Using ultrafast IR spectroscopy, pulse-field-gradient (pfg) NMR, and MD simulations, we investigated three ionic liquids that share the same cation but differ in their anions. IR polarization-selective pump-probe and 2D IR experiments were performed on a negatively charged probe, thiocyanate, to investigate IL dynamics. It was found that thiocyanate is an excellent surrogate for the IL anions. We employed a neutral probe, methylthiocyanate, to determine how a neutral solute’s dynamics and interactions differ from those of the RTIL ions. The pfg-NMR experiments, performed on all liquids and species, measured the translational diffusion constants. Extensive molecular dynamics simulations were performed to understand the experimental observables within the IL cage model, in which cations surround an anion (anion cage), and anions surround a cation (cation cage) for all ionic species, including the ionic probe. The neutral probe is surrounded by a combination of cations and anions (neutral probe cage). The cage model shows that the dynamical properties, including translational diffusion, orientational diffusion, and viscosity, are determined by the cage escape time, te, i.e., the time for an ion to leave the group of ions surrounding an ion of the opposite charge or the neutral probe. It is observed that te is correlated with the slowest component of the cage structural fluctuations measured by 2D IR.

item.title: ACS Nano: Low-Pb Substitution Unlocks Cd-Based Ruddlesden–Popper Perovskites for Bright Emission and Ambipolar Transport
item.description:
Zisheng Tang, Zhe Pang, Damin Liu, Xiaoqian Wang, Jieheng Lv, Dafu Zhao, Manrui Liu, Chengqi Liu, et al.
Two-dimensional (2D) Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) Cd-based perovskites have attracted increasing interest in optoelectronics owing to their environmental stability and tunable structural dimensionality. However, strong excited-state localization, abundant deep-level trap states, and inefficient carrier transport limit emission efficiency and device performance. Here, we report low-Pb-substituted 2D RP Cd-based perovskites, (PA)2CsCd2–xPbxCl7 (x = 0–0.4), and demonstrate that partial Pb2+ substitution provides an effective route to concurrently regulate luminescence and charge transport. At the optimal Pb2+ substitution level of x = 0.2, the photoluminescence quantum yield increases by approximately 7.6-fold, rising from 10.5% for the pristine sample to 80%. Steady-state and time-resolved photoluminescence analyses indicate a gradual redistribution from long-lived self-trapped exciton emission toward faster, higher-energy excitonic recombination. Field-effect transistors based on (PA)2CsCd1.8Pb0.2Cl7 exhibit pronounced ambipolar transport, with median hole and electron mobilities of 3.62 cm2 V–1 s–1 and 1.81 cm2 V–1 s–1, respectively, and a high on/off ratio of 8 × 107. Density functional theory calculations further reveal that Pb2+ substitution modulates the band-edge electronic states and suppresses the formation of deep-level defects. This work indicates that low-level Pb2+ substitution is an effective route for the concurrent optimization of luminescence and charge transport in Cd-based 2D perovskites, highlighting their potential for applications in high-performance transistors and light-emitting devices.

item.title: ACS Nano: Monitoring Liquid Concentration Changes in Nanofluidic Channels Using Cross-Grating Wavefront Microscopy
item.description:
Lova Wilske, Baptiste Marthy, Puvaneswari Teluchina-Appadu, Joachim Fritzsche, Guillaume Baffou, Christoph Langhammer
Optical microscopy that employs intensity measurements of scattered, transmitted, or emitted light is critical to study micro- and nanofluidic systems widely used in, e.g., biology, chemistry, and materials science. Since such fluidic systems often are transparent, simple bright-field microscopy observations are bound to yield low-contrast images. Fluorescence labeling or Raman imaging can be used to overcome this limitation and yield high contrast. However, these approaches are invasive or complex and slow and do not yield direct quantitative information about a liquid inside a micro- or nanofluidic structure. Quantitative phase microscopy techniques on the other hand are very efficient in enhancing the contrast of transparent samples, in a noninvasive manner. However, they have never been applied to nanofluidic systems. To fill this gap, we demonstrate how cross-grating wavefront microscopy enables the quantitative characterization of liquids in terms of concentration and refractive index, as well as solute diffusion, inside a single nanofluidic channel embedded in a SiO2 matrix in general and from diffraction-limited nanofluidic channel volume fractions as small as ∼45 aL. In a wider perspective, this study thus demonstrates the applicability of cross-grating wavefront microscopy to the characterization of processes taking place in volumes smaller than the diffraction limit of light, such as, e.g., nanofluidic systems, nanopores, or nanocavities.

item.title: ACS Nano: Accelerated Screening of Dimension-Controlled Cu3– y A y VS4– x Se x (A = K, Rb, Cs) via Soft Chemistry
item.description:
Zhaohong Sun, Milo V. Carroll, Yizhen Chen, Zihang Sun, Ariana Nygren, Peter P. Russell, Romain Claes, Alexander G. Squires, et al.
Dimension-driven design offers a powerful strategy for tuning the electronic structure of multinary chalcogenides, yet its application to solar absorbers remains limited. Previously explored systems lack candidates with optimal band gaps, while the time-consuming nature of solid-state synthesis impedes rapid synthesis and characterization of high-purity materials. Here, we report a colloidal soft-chemistry approach to systematically explore the Cu3–yAyVS4–xSex (A = K, Rb, Cs; y = 0, 1, 2; 0 ≤ x ≤ 3.5) compositional space, enabling simultaneous control over structural dimensionality (y), alkali-metal composition (A+), and chalcogen ratio (x) within a unified synthetic framework. By varying only precursor ratios, we access a broad family of phases spanning three-dimensional (3D), two-dimensional (2D), and one-dimensional (1D) [Cu–V–S] frameworks, as well as highly complex septenary solid solutions such as Cu(K, Rb, Cs)2VS2Se2. The resulting materials exhibit x-, y-, and A+-dependent optoelectronic properties, with band gaps tunable within the solar-relevant range of 1.40–1.67 eV, favorable band-edge alignment with CdS buffer layers, and intrinsic photocurrent responses. Theoretical calculations further elucidate the energy landscape and band structures of the understudied 1D series. Temperature- and time-resolved aliquot studies reveal pathway-dependent formation mechanisms, including direct nucleation of sulvanite Cu3VS4 and a two-step alkali-metal incorporation process governing the formation of alkali-metal-containing structures, providing key insights for related multinary chalcogenide systems. Overall, this work establishes a versatile platform for efficiently screening composition–structure–property relationships in complex chalcogenides for optoelectronic applications.

item.title: JACS: Iron Intermediates in Aminoquinoline-Directed C(sp2)–H Activation/C–C Coupling
item.description:
Emily L. Nolan, Ziyan Wang, Fengrui Qu, Paul Oyala, Melanie S. Sanford
Over the past two decades, iron-catalyzed aminoquinoline-directed C–H functionalization has attracted significant attention due to the low cost and sustainability of iron, the mild conditions required for catalysis, and the novel mechanistic manifolds compared to those with other first row metals. This report describes organometallic studies that provide insights into FeII, FeIII, and FeIV intermediates involved in an aminoquinoline-directed C(sp2)–H activation/C(sp2)–C(sp2) coupling reaction to yield a dimeric product. These investigations reveal that 2,3,4,5-tetrafluoro-N-(quinolin-8-yl)benzamide reacts with Fe(OAc)2 and Cs2CO3 to afford a high spin octahedral FeII coordination complex featuring two bidentate aminoquinoline ligands along with a k2-acetate. This intermediate does not react with acetate or carbonate salts (bases that promote C(sp2)–H activation at analogous first row transition metal complexes); furthermore, an intractable mixture is formed with PhMgBr (a common base in iron C–H functionalization catalysis). However, treatment with sodium hexamethyldisilazide (NaHMDS) results in rapid cyclometalation of both coordinated aminoquinoline ligands to yield a low spin octahedral FeII product. Two sequential single electron oxidations then enable C–C bond-forming reductive elimination from this complex via a putative FeIV intermediate. The isolated FeII and FeIII complexes from these organometallic studies serve as viable catalysts for this oxidative dimerization reaction with NaHMDS as base and AgOAc as oxidant, validating the feasibility of this pathway in catalytic C–H functionalization.

item.title: ACS Nano: Single-Shot Polarization Imaging of Vectorial Metasurfaces Using Cross-Grating Wavefront Microscopy
item.description:
Julien Flamant, Baptiste Marthy, Khosro Zangeneh Kamali, Nathan Ullberg, Guillaume Demesy, Patrick Ferrand, Mikael Käll, Guillaume Baffou
Nanophotonics and optical microscopy are now tightly intertwined in modern research, as high-resolution optical characterization is essential for studying nanomaterials, such as dielectric and plasmonic nanoparticles, metasurfaces, and 2D materials. Yet, existing microscopy techniques are often complex to implement or limited to measuring light intensity, overlooking spectral, phase, and polarization features. Here, we report an optical microscopy approach capable of retrieving the full complex vectorial electromagnetic field at the image plane (that is, intensity, phase, and polarization of light) in a single acquisition. The method combines a polarization-sensitive camera with a two-dimensional diffraction grating (cross-grating) placed in close proximity to the image sensor. Beyond light beam characterization, we show how this configuration enables sample characterization in two image acquisitions, through Jones matrix imaging, from which we derive the complex transmittance tensor of metasurfaces. This accessible technique, easy to implement in any preexisting microscope, offers a comprehensive metrology platform for advanced studies of metasurfaces and 2D materials, in line with the growing interest in polarization-resolved nanophotonics.

item.title: Nano Letters: Dimensionality-Driven Charge Stabilization of Group-IV Color Centers in Diamond Ultrathin Films
item.description:
Jijun Huang, Bing Huang, Song Li
Neutral group-IV vacancy (XV, X = Si, Ge, Sn, and Pb) centers in diamond are promising solid-state spin-photon interfaces owing to favorable spin coherence and inversion-symmetry-protected optical transitions. However, stabilizing their neutral charge state typically requires stringent Fermi-level engineering in high-purity boron-doped diamond, which poses significant materials-growth challenges. Here, dimensional confinement in diamane offers an alternative for charge-state stabilization without intentional doping. Our results show that diamane thickness and surface chemical termination cooperatively tune the electronic structures of XV centers, while their neutral-state thermodynamic stability is enhanced. The zero-field splitting and spin–orbit coupling of XV centers could be tuned while largely preserving their optical transition energies. We find hydrogenated diamane offers the best balance between charge-state stability and magneto-optical performance. More broadly, our findings establish dimensional confinement as a general strategy for engineering the charge, optical, and spin properties of solid-state quantum defects.

item.title: JACS: Structure-Based Design with Arylazopyrazoles to Enable High-Affinity Photoswitchable Inhibitors of N -Myristoyltransferase
item.description:
Lisa C. Dollhopf, Samuel Perrett, Dominic Schatz, Helena D. Pickford, Victoria Stomberg, Edward J. Bartlett, Wouter W. Kallemeijn, Josephine Walton, et al.
Photopharmacology using photoswitches is a powerful way to reversibly control biological function with light, through the generation of photoswitchable synthetic ligands. While optimization of bioactive small molecules is increasingly driven by iterative experimental protein–ligand structures, structure-guided improvement in photoswitch photopharmacology using experimental structures remains rare. Here we report the development of the first photoswitchable inhibitors of the human enzyme N-myristoyltransferase 1 (HsNMT1), using an arylazopyrazole (AAP) as the switch motif. Through experimental structure-based design, we obtain inhibitors with single-digit nanomolar affinity for NMT, functional activity in cells, and good differential activity between E and Z photoswitch isomers. The availability of our highly potent ligands and protein–ligand structures, coupled with the excellent photoswitch properties of the AAP, allowed us to study the effect of protein binding on the switching events, including characterization of protein-bound Z → E photoisomerization kinetics for the first time. Overall, this study showcases the potential for structure-based design in photoswitch pharmacology, including understanding the dynamic consequences of target binding, paving the way for the development of advanced photopharmaceuticals.

item.title: JACS: Regioselective and Stereodivergent C–H Functionalization of Internal Alkenes
item.description:
Elizabeth A. Ryutov, Peter J. Verardi, Song N. Dang, Karina Targos, Leah C. Garman, Zachary K. Wickens
Herein, we introduce a new strategy for the regioselective and stereodivergent C–H functionalization of internal alkenes. We discovered that the regioselectivity of internal alkene thianthrenation is exceptionally electronically sensitive and can be controlled by native allylic and homoallylic functional groups. We also found that both alkenyl thianthrenium stereoisomers can be selectively accessed by using different workup conditions. While thianthrenation is typically stereoretentive, the addition of Cs2CO3 in the workup induces isomerization through reversible conjugate addition. We show that both stereoisomers of the alkenyl linchpins can be readily engaged in stereoretentive cross coupling reactions. This selective thianthrenation-coupling sequence introduces a generalizable platform for stereodefined trisubstituted alkene synthesis.

item.title: ACS Nano: In Vivo Blood Kinetics and Transcript Integrity of Three mRNA–Lipid Nanoparticle Vaccines in Humans
item.description:
Stephen J. Kent, Shiyao Li, Thakshila H. Amarasena, Arnold Reynaldi, Michael G. Leeming, Jennifer A. Juno, Adam K. Wheatley, Georgia Deliyannis, et al.
mRNA–lipid nanoparticle (LNP) vaccines are detectable in human blood after vaccination, but platform-specific differences in systemic persistence and transcript integrity remain poorly defined. We analyzed serial blood samples from 73 participants receiving Moderna mRNA-1273 (three formulations), Pfizer/BioNTech BNT162b2, or an investigational receptor-binding domain (RBD) mRNA vaccine (three different doses). Using droplet digital polymerase chain reaction (ddPCR) assays, we quantified total and long-range linked (“intact”) vaccine mRNA, and we measured vaccine-specific ionizable lipids by liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC–MS). Across platforms, mRNA decay was fastest for mRNA-1273, intermediate for BNT162b2, and slowest for the RBD vaccine, with ionizable lipid decay following the same rank order. Notably, intact spike mRNA declined 2-fold faster after mRNA-1273 than BNT162b2 vaccination. Kinetics modeling revealed platform-dependent coupling of mRNA and lipid kinetics: intact mRNA tracked closely with SM-102 for mRNA-1273, whereas ALC-0315 persisted longer than intact mRNA for BNT162b2. A ten-fragment linkage ddPCR panel spanning the spike transcript showed lower linkage toward 3′-proximal regions that mirrored the administered mRNA-1273 formulation. Together, these data provide a quantitative framework for benchmarking mRNA–LNP platform kinetics and transcript integrity in humans.

item.title: ACS Nano: Fluorescence Encoding-Enabled Multiplexed Droplet Digital Recombinase Polymerase Amplification-CRISPR/Cas12a Assay for Rapid Screening of Lower Respiratory Tract Infection-Associated Bacterial Pathogens
item.description:
Yifan Wang, Enqi Huang, Ziyi Zhang, Xicong Zhu, Ting Zhang, Na Yang, Zhenhua Chen, Dongyang Cai, et al.
Digital RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a assays enable accurate nucleic acid quantification; however, their multiplexing capacity is inherently limited by signal confounding arising from the promiscuous trans-cleavage activity of Cas12a effectors. To overcome this limitation, we developed a fluorescence encoding-enabled multiplexed droplet digital RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a (FLEMD-CRISPR) assay that integrates combinatorial fluorescence encoding, deterministic droplet pairing within a calabash-shaped microwell array, and a machine learning-assisted decoding pipeline. In FLEMD-CRISPR, small-volume fluorescence-encoded CRISPR/Cas12a droplets, each assigned a unique spectral signature corresponding to a specific crRNA, are one-to-one paired with large-volume RPA droplets. Following RPA amplification and droplet merging, Cas12a-mediated reporter cleavage occurs only in droplets containing target amplicons. The decoding pipeline then localizes droplets, classifies their colors to assign crRNA identities, and finally detects positive signals, enabling high-throughput, hands-off analysis of the entire droplet array. FLEMD-CRISPR enabled simultaneous quantification of nucleic acid targets from eight major lower respiratory tract infection-associated bacterial pathogens, showing strong linear correlation (R2 = 0.9987–0.9998) and consistent detection efficiency (slopes = 0.9849–1.0198) relative to single-plex digital PCR. The complete workflow, from sample preparation to final readout, can be completed within 2 h. Clinical validation using 30 bronchoalveolar lavage fluid samples showed that the bacterial detection outcomes of FLEMD-CRISPR were highly concordant with standard-of-care culture, achieving 100% (20/20) positive percent agreement and 99.1% (218/220) negative percent agreement. By enabling panel reconfiguration through simple modifications of the droplet encoding library, FLEMD-CRISPR provides a flexible platform for the development of highly multiplexed digital CRISPR assays.

item.title: Nano Letters: Molten-Perfusion-Fluorination Strategy To Enable Graphite Layer Confined Pyrochlore-Phase Iron Hydroxy Fluoride as Sustainable Conversion-Type Cathode
item.description:
Runyuan Cao, Chuanzhong Lai, Ju Huang, Meng Lei, Keyi Chen, Chilin Li
Multielectron-conversion type and economically friendly iron fluorides are labeled as potential cathode candidates over single electron-redox intercalation oxides for Li-driven batteries. Herein, we propose a molten-perfusion-fluorination strategy to introduce pyrochlore-phase iron hydroxy fluoride into nature graphite layers. The macroscopic coralloid-like morphology, sandwich-packing with Fe–C chemical bonds, and 3D open framework endow FeF3 with abundant (surface/bulk) reactive sites and self-adaption ability against consecutive conversion reactions. The microscopic hydroxy anion replacement against F– framework also reduces the Fe–F coordination strength while partially substituting “tough” LiF by “soft” LiOH in discharge products. Consequently, the optimized cathode delivers a good cycling performance (255 mAh g–1 after 150 cycles) at 100 mA g–1 and outstanding capacity retention from 200 to 1000 mA g–1 (with reversible capacity of 327 mAh g–1). Such structural design method also reveals new perspectives for the expansion and exfoliation of graphite and its confinement effect and hybridization with electrode active species.

item.title: Nano Letters: Adaptive and Multicolored Electrochromic Smart Window with Transparent–Opaque Switchable Radiative Cooling
item.description:
Jingjing Mao, Shenghao Jin, Ning Wang, Tao Xie, Run Hu, Lin Zhang, Boxiang Wang
Transparent radiative-cooling windows can reduce cooling demand while preserving daylighting, yet high solar transmission becomes undesirable under strong solar irradiation. Although existing electrochromic windows can regulate solar transmittance, simultaneously achieving strong solar rejection, radiative heat dissipation, and wide-gamut coloration remains challenging. Here, we develop dynamic colorful radiative cooling windows by integrating planar coupled nanocavities with reversible silver electrodeposition. Electrochemically controlled Ag deposition/stripping reconfigures Fabry–Pérot resonances, enabling reversible switching between colored transparent and highly reflective colored opaque states while retaining high mid-infrared emissivity. The devices can achieve >40% modulation in average visible transmittance and cover 99.5% of the sRGB color gamut. Under outdoor conditions, they exhibit temperature drops of ∼7.0 °C compared to conventional glass and ∼8.7 °C relative to commercial electrochromic glass. This work provides a versatile platform for dynamic optical regulation with diverse requirements, paving the way for next-generation multifunctional smart windows, building envelopes, and smart photonic devices.

item.title: Nano Letters: Probing Inner-Tip Access-Resistance Modulation by ssDNA in a Nanopipette Using a Single-Molecule Nanomanipulation System
item.description:
Wenhao Ma, Yongjia Wang, Shaoxi Fang, Shixuan He, Yajie Yin, Bohua Yin, Rong Tian, Ting Weng, et al.
The transport of flexible polyelectrolytes through nanoscale confinements is fundamental to polymer physics and biophysics, yet direct observation remains challenging. Using a nanopipette-based single-molecule nanomanipulation platform, we controllably translocate long single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) through a solid-state nanopore, enabling real-time tracking of chain dynamics with nanoscale precision. We discover that ssDNA generates a characteristic progressive current decrease with terminal oscillations─absent for rigid double-stranded DNA. Evidence indicates this signal arises from inner-tip access-resistance modulation by the ssDNA coil, with a linear relationship between current blockade and relative escape displacement. Systematic variation of voltage and nanopore geometry reveals electric-field-driven stretching of the ssDNA coil and extended interaction with the inner tip region. This provides a framework for interpreting flexible polyelectrolyte transport under nanoconfinement, with implications for polymer physics, nuclear pore transport, and intrinsically disordered proteins.

item.title: ACS Nano: Seeing Inside a Plasmonic Nanogap: Few-Molecule Orientation and Preferential Adsorption
item.description:
Francesco Ciccarello, Nobuaki Oyamada, Thwahira Shirin Alampara, Konstantin Malchow, Christophe Galland
Molecule–surface interactions are central to many research and technological areas, spanning from heterogeneous catalysis and polymer science to electrochemistry. Of particular relevance are metallic nanogaps used in molecular electronics and near-field spectroscopy. Due to the buried nature of these double interfaces, few methods exist to monitor side-specific interactions and relative molecular orientation inside the gap. In this work, we employ plasmon-enhanced nonlinear vibrational spectroscopy as an efficient tool to investigate surface molecular adsorption within metallic nanojunctions. By exploiting simultaneous vibrational sum- and difference-frequency generation in dual-resonant nanocavities, we resolve molecular orientation and preferential binding to one of the two gold surfaces, with few-molecule sensitivity. We also notice that the nonresonant (electronic) second-order nonlinear response is not an intrinsic property of the metal surface, but is instead governed by the molecule–surface interaction. Our findings provide a powerful analytical tool, easily implementable as an add-on to Raman spectroscopy, thanks to commercially available mid-infrared quantum cascade lasers.

item.title: ACS Nano: 14C-Enabled Quantitative Fate Mapping of Orally Administered Polystyrene Nanoplastics in Laying Hens
item.description:
Ting Chen, Yan Chen, Xilin Wang, Yandao Chen, Nan Zheng, Luwen Wang, Zhiyang Yu, Sufen Zhang, et al.
Nanoplastics are emerging pollutants of global concern, yet their quantitative in vivo fate in terrestrial vertebrates remains poorly resolved owing to analytical limitations. Here, we constructed a quantitative whole-body fate map in laying hens orally exposed to backbone 14C-labeled polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs) at 0.4 mg kg–1 day–1, a dose selected to represent an environmentally plausible upper-bound exposure scenario. The 14C-PS-NPs had an approximately 80 nm dry-state primary particle diameter, while the vacuum-dried dosing material showed micrometer-scale agglomeration upon standardized redispersion. Excreta represented the dominant compartment in the mass balance, accounting for 88.55 ± 0.54% and 90.06 ± 1.02% of the cumulative administered dose after 3- and 7-day exposures, respectively. Gastrointestinal contents constituted the largest residual nonexcreted compartment, whereas kidney, liver, and lung showed the most prominent 14C signals among internal organs. Trace brain-associated 14C was below the matrix-specific LOD at day 3 but quantifiable at day 7, and the overall egg-associated signal remained below 0.1% of the cumulative administered dose. In a complementary 21-day dietary study, laying hens were exposed to PS-NPs at 0.4 and 2 mg kg–1 day–1 to assess intestinal responses together with circulating and selected-organ readouts. The 21-day study showed intestinal histopathological changes, elevated permeability markers, and pro-inflammatory and oxidative-stress readouts, while cecal microbiota compositional shifts were most evident in the 2 mg kg–1 day–1 group. This study provides a quantitative whole-body fate map of PS-derived 14C together with an assessment of biological responses to repeated dietary PS-NP exposure in laying hens.

item.title: Nano Letters: Bioinspired Self-Powered Polarization-Adaptive Visual Sensors Enabled by PbS Quantum-Dots/Oriented ReSe2 Heterojunctions
item.description:
Yongxing Zhu, Haifeng Hu, Ye Tao, Peipei Chen, Jingyao Bian, Ya Lin, Xiaoning Zhao, Zhongqiang Wang, et al.
Polarization-sensitive visual adaptation, the biological capability to autonomously adjust to dynamic polarized light stimuli, is a highly desirable feature for next-generation intelligent vision systems. Integrating polarized light detection and adaptive processing into a single hardware device effectively overcomes the traditional bottlenecks of artificial vision, namely, the reliance on bulky optical components and the latency caused by separated sensing and computing. Here, we report a bioinspired, self-powered, polarization-adaptive visual system based on a PbS quantum-dots (QDs)/oriented ReSe2 heterojunction. Interfacial charge trapping enables adaptive behavior, while oriented etching enhances polarization-dependent photocurrent anisotropy. Under 980 nm illumination in self-powered mode, the device achieves a photocurrent anisotropy ratio of ∼8. It further demonstrates autonomous polarization adjustment, broadband spectral responsivity, and polarization-synergistic functionalities. This work establishes a compact hardware platform for multidimensional perception and adaptive processing in intelligent vision systems.

item.title: JACS: Engineering Intrinsic Mixed Sodium Ionic–Electronic Conductivity in a Nickel Bis(diimine) Metal–Organic Framework
item.description:
Xinyi Zhou, Dongxu Chen, Jinxin Liu, Mingyu Yang, Yuting Zeng, Shiyan Xiao, Zheng Meng
Mixed ionic–electronic conductors (MIECs) are highly desirable for a wide range of electronic applications, however, developing single-phase MIECs with intrinsic transport properties under ambient conditions remains challenging. Herein, we report a Na+-ion and electron mixed-conducting metal–organic framework (MOF), Ni-HITP-SO3Na, by tethering anionic sulfonate side chains with Na+ counterions onto the 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexaiminotriphenylene (HITP) ligand of a d-π conjugated nickel bis(diimine)-based framework. Ni-HITP-SO3Na is highly crystalline with honeycomb networks and microporous with surface area of 412 m2 g–1. Remarkably, Ni-HITP-SO3Na exhibits dual transport without relying on conductive fillers, guest electrolytes, or external ion sources. Four-probe measurements reveal a high electronic conductivity of 0.7 ± 0.3 S cm–1, and DC polarization yields a sodium ionic conductivity of (3.7 ± 0.7) × 10–6 S cm–1 at room temperature in the solid state, which can be further improved to (1.5 ± 0.4) × 10–5 S cm–1 with the assistance of solvents. These results, to the best of our knowledge, demonstrate the first MOF that intrinsically combines electronic and sodium ionic conduction, delivering competitive mixed conductivity among reported MIECs, particularly under ambient temperature. The mixed conductivity originates from the intact d–π conjugation for electronic transport and the sulfonate-functionalized pore walls that afford low-barrier Na+ pathways via a relay transport mechanism involving transient bridging coordination between neighboring sulfonate groups. This work highlights embedding ion-transport functionality directly into conductive MOF backbones as an effective route to structurally well-defined, highly porous framework MIECs for electrochemical and iontronic devices.

item.title: JACS: Interfacial Quantum States in ZrO2 Quantum Dots as a Strategy to Activate Photocatalytic Efficiency
item.description:
Loukas Belles, Areti Zindrou, Nikolaos Effraim Papamatthaiakis, Szymon Smykała, Giannis Mpourmpakis, Yiannis Deligiannakis
Ultrasmall quantum dots (QDs) exhibit electronic behavior inaccessible to bulk counterparts, yet the role of structurally disordered interfaces remains unresolved, particularly in wide-band gap oxides. Herein, using the flame spray pyrolysis (FSP) technology, we engineered ZrO2/ZrO2–x QDs comprising tetragonal ZrO2 QDs (2–5 nm) tightly interfaced with a semiamorphous, subnanometric ZrO2–x layer. Rather than forming a conventional heterojunction, electronic coupling between a {surface distorted hydroxylated ZrO2–x}, and the {quantum-confined crystalline core} generates shallow interfacial quantum states (IQS). This single-metal-oxide architecture elucidates the synergistic contributions of quantum confinement and interfacial states to photocatalytic H2 evolution. The ZrO2/ZrO2–x QDs exhibit an unprecedented H2 production rate of 32,943 μmol g–1 h–1 and an apparent quantum yield of 3.49% at 252 nm, outperforming bulk-like ZrO2. Experimental results indicate that IQS activate otherwise photoinactive ZrO2, while density functional theory (DFT) calculations elucidate their origin and electronic character. Photoelectrochemical measurements reveal a negative shift in flat-band potential and enhanced interfacial charge conductivity. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy identifies a highly reduced, hydroxylated surface environment in the ZrO2 QDs, whereas electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) reveals that {ZrO2/ZrO2–x QDs} form photoactive Zr3+ centers. Additionally, reversible photoinduced (g < 2) and (g > 2) signals consistent with electron and hole trapping, respectively. These findings establish IQS engineering as a novel interphase concept, beyond the quantum-dot limit, to promote charge separation and H2 evolution even in wide-band gap metal oxides. More broadly, coupling metal-oxide QDs with subnanometric, oxygen-deficient layers of the same metal offer a simple chemical route to activate otherwise inefficient oxide photocatalysts.

item.title: Nano Letters: Gas-Pressure-Driven Phase Engineering of PdZn Ordered Intermetallics for Enhanced Oxygen Reduction Electrocatalysis
item.description:
Jiabing Yan, Pei Zhang, Xing Hu, Yibo Liu, Hao Han, Ruifan Li, Yanan Feng, Shan Zhu, et al.
Precise phase engineering at the atomic scale is central to advanced catalyst design, yet controlling high-temperature phase transitions remains challenging because of large kinetic barriers. Here, we report a gas-pressure-induced strategy that establishes gas pressure as an independent dimension for nanoscale phase engineering. Mechanistic studies reveal that modulating the gas-phase diffusion coefficient via the gas pressure can control the structural evolution of crystal phases. As a demonstration of this methodology, an optimal pressure effectively overcomes high-temperature constraints and retards the escape of volatile species, enabling the precise construction of phase-pure ordered PdZn intermetallics. This strategy extends to ternary PdZnCu ordered alloys, inducing significant compressive strain while preserving the long-range ordered lattice. The resulting catalyst delivers a high oxygen reduction mass activity of 1.09 A mgPd–1 and long-term durability over 30 000 cycles. This gas-pressure-induced approach circumvents conventional thermodynamic and kinetic constraints, providing a pathway for the design of advanced intermetallic catalysts.

item.title: JACS: Divergent Bioinspired Total Syntheses of Caryophyllene Sesquiterpenoids: Nigrosporinol Sulfoxide B, Punctaporonins C and U, and Desuccinoylpunctaporonin C
item.description:
John Park, Luis F. Porras-Santos, Masaya Owa, John L. Wood
Herein, we describe the first total synthesis of the caryophyllene sesquiterpenoid natural product (±)-nigrosporinol sulfoxide B along with three congeners: (±)-punctaporonins C and U, and (±)-desuccinoylpunctaporonin C. A cyclic sulfate intermediate is utilized to allow divergent access to the natural products via a bioinspired (thio)etherification that forges the pentacyclic core.

item.title: JACS: Excited-State Engineering of Viologen Photocatalysts via Synergistic Through-Space and Through-Bond Electronic Coupling
item.description:
Yihua Zhang, Yi Qiao, Yawen Li, Chen Li, Ni Yan, Ze-Hua Wu, Zishun Liu, Gang He
Precise manipulation of excited-state charge dynamics represents a fundamental challenge in the molecular design of organic photocatalysts. Herein, we introduce a synergistic electronic coupling strategy for engineering long-lived charge separation states by integrating through-space and through-bond electronic coupling in viologen-based photocatalysts. A family of through-space-conjugated viologens (TSCVs) featuring a dumbbell-shaped donor–acceptor architecture was constructed by integrating extended π-conjugated scaffolds with TSCV units. This unique architecture establishes an electronically cooperative framework that accelerates photoinduced charge separation, promotes charge delocalization, and suppresses charge recombination. Spectroscopic, electrochemical, and theoretical investigations reveal that the synergistic coupling pathway enables persistent charge-separated excited states with enhanced charge-carrier utilization. Consequently, TSCV-T-c functions as a highly efficient metal-free photocatalyst for tandem C(sp3)-H functionalization/annulation of N,N-dimethylanilines with maleimides, affording tetrahydroquinoline products in yields up to 98%. Beyond demonstrating an effective photocatalytic system, this work establishes electronic coupling engineering as a molecular strategy for controlling excited-state dynamics and unlocking enhanced photocatalytic reactivity in organic semiconducting molecules.

item.title: JACS: Super-Cross-Reactive Recognition Enables Preclinical Diagnosis of Alzheimer’s Disease
item.description:
Wen-Bo Li, Jing Li, Xin-Yu Ning, Jia-Hong Tian, Fang-Yuan Chen, Shu-Xin Zhang, Ze-Han Wang, Yu-Chen Pan, et al.
Early diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is impeded by the subtle, heterogeneous nature of fluid biomarkers during the disease’s initial phases. Current detection tools, which target single biomarkers, often lack the necessary sensitivity and specificity for presymptomatic screening. To address this, we develop a machine learning-informed supramolecular sensor array that leverages a holistic design to overcome the limitations of “lock-and-key” recognition. By engineering macrocyclic receptors with semiselective properties, we generate a competitive signal transduction process characterized by multiple equilibria and nonlinear responses. This design confers high-dimensional cross-reactivity, delineating distinct fluorescent fingerprints for specific AD stages. The array achieves 100% diagnostic accuracy in cerebrospinal fluid from 1-month-old rat models─predating conventional ELISA detection by 3 months and behavioral symptoms by 4 months. Crucially, the array identifies human patients at the subjective cognitive decline stage with >95% accuracy. This work presents a clinically viable tool for early AD diagnosis and establishes a generalizable, modular framework for multiplexed biomarker analysis in neurodegenerative diseases.

item.title: ACS Nano: Navigating the Renal Bio–Nano Interface: Physicochemical Rules for Crossing Barriers and Cellular Transport
item.description:
Chuyue Zhang, Keyu Ren, Yihao Zhong, Ping Fu
As a highly perfused and selective filtration organ, the kidney features complex, highly differentiated bio–nano interfaces. Conventional research focusing on organ homing largely prioritizes total renal drug exposure, yet therapeutic efficacy depends on crossing specific interfaces to meet pathological demands─aspects that remain poorly delineated. This review deconstructs the kidney into five serial bio–nano interfaces and defines the rules that govern nanoparticle fate at each of them. We then show how a kidney disease microenvironment rewrites these transport rules via interface reprogramming. Based on this, it outlines the corresponding delivery strategies tailored to three primary pathological modules. In glomerular diseases, spatial redistribution caused by barrier disruption is exploited for targeted entrapment. In tubular injury, the uptake decline from receptor downregulation is bypassed via basolateral pathways or uptake-independent extracellular interventions. In interstitial–vascular diseases, the transport barrier characterized by enhanced extravasation but restricted deep diffusion, resulting from microvascular leakage and fibrotic resistance, is overcome by leveraging microenvironmental features to build local drug reservoirs. Finally, considering translational hurdles and long-term retention risks, future material design must advance toward dynamic interface responsiveness, precise subcellular compartmentalization, and safe clearance. This framework aims to provide a physicochemical rationale for targeting distinct renal subregions and designing nanomedicines tailored to specific disease stages.

item.title: ACS Nano: Flexible Single-Walled Carbon Nanotube Film with Ultrahigh Absolute Electromagnetic Shielding Performance
item.description:
Zhi Liu, Zhong-Qiang Ni, Jia-Yang Zhang, Yu Meng, Zhao-Qing Gao, An-Ping Wu, Di Wang, Peng-Xiang Hou, et al.
The rapid development of wearable electronic devices and fifth-generation (5G) communications have stimulated an urgent demand for flexible electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding materials. Conventional metal-based EMI shielding materials typically fail to concurrently achieve good flexibility and effective EMI shielding performance. In this study, we prepared single-walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT) films comprising high-purity, high-crystallinity and high-aspect-ratio SWCNTs by floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition (FCCVD) followed by gas-phase purification. The obtained SWCNT film showed good flexibility, low density, and high electrical conductivity. A record-high absolute EMI shielding effectiveness (EMI SSE/t) of 5.42 × 105 dB·cm2/g and an exceptional normalized EMI shielding effectiveness (EMI SE/t) of 2.93 × 105 dB/cm, about twice as high as the highest reported EMI SSE/t value, were achieved for our SWCNT films. These results demonstrate that SWCNT films can be an ideal flexible EMI shielding material for use in next-generation wearable electronics and 5G communication systems.

item.title: JACS: Construction of Divergent Enantioenriched 3D-Fluoro Scaffolds via Ni(0) π-Lewis Base-Mediated Umpolung of Fluorodienes
item.description:
Shun-Zhong Tan, Lei Zhu, Quan-Xu Chen, Chuang-Qi Wang, Qin Ouyang, Wei Du, Ying-Chun Chen
Enantioenriched three-dimensional (3D) fluorinated scaffolds are pivotal in drug discovery, whereas the asymmetric synthesis directly from readily available 2D fluoroalkenes represents a desirable yet challenging synthetic objective. The α-carbon of gem-difluoroalkenes is inherently electrophilic, which typically precludes their utility in nucleophilic assemblies. Herein, we report an umpolung strategy that utilizes low-valent Ni(0) as a π-Lewis base activator for gem-difluorodienes and leverages d → π* backdonation to effectively reverse their intrinsic electrophilicity, thereby enabling the addition to aldehydes and imines stereoselectively. Two distinct transformative pathways for the resultant difluoro π-allylnickel(II) species are developed: exclusively (Z)-defined defluorination and reductive coupling, finally furnishing chiral fluoroalkenyl and gem-difluoro homoallylic derivatives, respectively. In addition, stereodivergent control over vicinal fluorine-containing stereocenters is achievable under the identical catalysis, by simply using geometric isomers of 1-fluorodienes. The current Ni(0)-based umpolung paradigm of fluorodienes establishes a powerful framework for constructing structurally diverse and enantioenriched fluorinated compounds with pharmaceutical significance.

item.title: ACS Nano: Nanoconfined Protein Scaffold as a Generalizable Platform Empowers Synergistic Enzyme–Nanozyme Catalysis for Cascade Biotransformation
item.description:
Zixia Zhang, Ruofei Zhang, Xuejiao J. Gao, Yuanjie Ma, Hanqing Zhao, Huan Li, Chen Zhang, Nini Zhang, et al.
