These results establish SQD-AIMD and SQD-vibrational analysis as practical and scalable frameworks for simulating chemical reaction dynamics and elucidating reaction mechanisms on near-term quantum hardware, extending quantum computing applications beyond static electronic structure calculations.

item.title: ACS Nano: Wearable Sweat Biosystem with Dual Diffusion-Limiting Interface for Dynamic Hyperlactatemia Management in Critical Care
item.description:
Yunxiang Long, Xiaosen Pan, Yao Chen, Nanpei Li, Wentong Wang, Yuqi Wang, Wanyu Zhang, Taozhe Liu, et al.
Hyperlactatemia is a critical indicator of tissue hypoperfusion, metabolic dysfunction, and an adverse prognosis in critically ill patients. Yet conventional monitoring depends entirely on intermittent, invasive blood sampling, which cannot capture the dynamic metabolic fluctuations required to guide timely clinical interventions. Herein, we report a wearable sweat-sensing device built on a dual-diffusion-limiting architecture for the continuous and accurate assessment of clinical hyperlactatemia. This system synergistically modulates lactate diffusion in sweat through a silane-network-encapsulated lactate oxidase layer coupled to a polyvinyl chloride layer. This design effectively delays enzyme saturation, extending the linear detection range for sweat lactate to 0–60 mM and thereby fulfilling the stringent requirements of critical care monitoring. The device also integrates real-time pH and temperature calibration to safeguard measurement accuracy in complex physiological environments. Moreover, linear mixed-effects analysis of 82 paired samples from 33 critically ill patients demonstrated a strong association between sweat and blood lactate levels, with a marginal R2 of 0.840. Sweat lactate effectively identified hyperlactatemia and predicted in-hospital mortality, yielding areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve values of 0.943 and 0.785, respectively. The integrated iontophoresis-microfluidics module further ensures high consistency with bedside arterial blood gas analysis, as validated by a marginal R2 of 0.811. Together, these results establish sweat biosensors as a promising platform for continuous metabolic monitoring, resuscitation assessment, and objective prognostic stratification in critical care settings.

item.title: JACS: Structural Rigidity Enables Amplified Spontaneous Emission in 2D Alkylammonium Tin Perovskites
item.description:
Francesca Canestra, Nurgul Sarsembek, Yarong He, Andrea Pianetti, Martina Santarelli, Silvia Contessi, Ranita Samanta, Martina Zangari, et al.
Two-dimensional tin perovskites are attracting increasing attention for coherent light emission, yet the impact of organic cations on their properties remains poorly understood. Here, we compare the Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) butylammonium tin iodide (BA2SnI4) and Dion–Jacobson (DJ) 1,4-diammoniobutane tin iodide (DABSnI4) perovskites to investigate the impact of the two structural types on their photophysical and optical gain properties. Combining X-ray diffraction and solid-state NMR spectroscopy, we reveal the different templating properties of the mono- and ditopic cations on the long-range structural order and local coordination environment, identifying an unreported phase transition for DABSnI4. The constrained molecular motions in the DJ perovskite provide an increased structural rigidity that also suppresses vibrational modes of the inorganic sublattice. The consequent lower exciton–phonon coupling and exciton binding energy, reduced defectivity, and modulation of the exciton recombination dynamics create favorable conditions to stabilize the population inversion and achieve amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) in DABSnI4, in net contrast with BA2SnI4 where ASE could not be obtained. This work highlights that Dion–Jacobson perovskites can create more rigid structural environments with positive feedback on the photophysical properties, providing a simple but effective design strategy for the synthesis of improved materials for optoelectronic applications.

item.title: JACS: An “Unachievable” Molecular Sieve with Sole Six-Membered Rings
item.description:
Jiaqi Shi, Zhipeng Li, Caiyi Lou, Rutang Cheng, Yi Zhai, Qinming Wu, Zhaochi Feng, Ye Ma, et al.
The frameworks of zeolite molecular sieves constructed from a sole type of ring, such as 6-membered rings (6MRs), are regarded as unachievable structures that would not even be found in hypothetical zeolite databases containing tens of millions of structures. Herein, we for the first time report a novel aluminophosphate ZJM-11 molecular sieve, with a fully 6-membered ring (6MR) framework, which was successfully obtained from topotactic transformation. The obtained structure, which possesses fully opened micropores, represents a rare case of a single-ring zeolite topology with an ultrahigh framework density, viewed from the perspective of conventional wisdom as an “unachievable” molecular sieve. Advanced characterizations unveil the dynamic framework reconstruction mediated by ZJM-9 and/or ZJM-10 intermediates, pinpointing this structural evolution as the essential step toward ZJM-11 formation. This work therefore delivers critical knowledge for the rational design of unconventional zeolite molecular sieves.

item.title: Nano Letters: Low-Dimensional Chiral Perovskites for Polarization-Sensitive Photodetection
item.description:
Kaichen Wang, Yu Zhou, Bori Shi, Xiaofei Sun, Xiao Qiu, Zhiyong Fan
Emerging low-dimensional chiral perovskites have recently demonstrated significant application potential in circularly polarized light detection, spintronics, and quantum information technology due to their unique chiroptical activity and spin-selective properties. This review systematically summarizes their material systems, synthesis methods, chirality transfer mechanisms, and applications in photodetectors. The critical role of chiral organic cations in crystal regulation and chiroptical properties along with corresponding fabrication strategies is analyzed. Then, the inherent mechanisms of chirality transfer from organic to inorganic components are thoroughly discussed, encompassing structural distortion induction and electronic orbital coupling. Subsequently, recent advances in circularly polarized photodetectors based on low-dimensional chiral perovskites are highlighted from device performance, spin selection efficiency, to bio-inspired polarization vision systems. Finally, the challenges and future directions in this field are prospected. This review provides a comprehensive summarization for the development of low-dimensional chiral perovskites and their applications in next-generation polarized photodetectors.

item.title: Nano Letters: Polyaniline-Modified MXene/Carbon Nanotube Scaffold Enabling High-Rate and Long-Cycle Zinc–Iodine Batteries
item.description:
Xiaoqian Gong, Yixing Wang, Mengya Ge, Qinghong Wang
Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn–I2) batteries are attractive for large-scale energy storage because of their low cost and inherent safety. However, the practical use of an I2 cathode is severely restricted by poor electronic conductivity and the shuttle effect of soluble polyiodides. Herein, a synergistic scaffold composed of MXene and carbon nanotubes (CNTs) modified with protonated polyaniline (PANI) via electrostatic interactions was designed. The MXene/CNT scaffold ensures overall conductivity and structural integrity. The protonated PANI immobilizes iodine species through nitrogen-containing groups and accelerates their interconversion, effectively suppressing the shuttle effect. The MXene/CNTs/PANI-I2 cathode with an iodine loading of 43.96 wt % achieves a superior specific capacity of 150 mAh g–1 at a high rate of 20 C as well as excellent cycling stability over 10 000 cycles. This work offers a viable strategy for developing stable I2 cathodes for high-performance Zn–I2 batteries.

item.title: Nano Letters: From Micro to Nano: Boosting γ-MnO2 Cathode Performance through Particle Size Engineering
item.description:
Ella Davidi, Isaac Loke, Samuel Eisenberg, Xinzhe Xue, Megan C. Freyman, Asya Orhan, Erika P. Ramos, Jianchao Ye, et al.
Fast-charging lithium-ion batteries require cathodes that sustain rapid Li+ transport while maintaining structural and interfacial stability. Here, we investigate particle-size effects in γ-MnO2 by comparing micron-sized (4.4 ± 0.8 μm) and nanosized (62 ± 21 nm) particles under identical conditions. Nanosized γ-MnO2 delivers 160.1 mAh g–1 at C/10 and retains ∼66% capacity at 5C while exhibiting lower charge-transfer and diffusion-related impedance. Cyclic voltammetry and Dunn’s analysis reveal a 68.9% capacitive contribution at 2 mV s–1, indicating a shift toward faster surface-controlled charge storage enabled by increased surface area and shorter Li+ diffusion pathways. GITT measurements show deeper lithiation (x ≈ 0.65 vs 0.48 in LixMnO2) and a more homogeneous solid-solution-like intercalation regime in nanosized particles, avoiding bulk phase-transition kinetic bottlenecks. The nanosized cathode retains 70% capacity with ∼99.5% Coulombic efficiency after 400 cycles at 3C, demonstrating particle-size engineering as an effective strategy for high-rate, long-life advanced battery energy storage.

item.title: JACS: A Multiscale Theoretical Framework of Piezocatalysis
item.description:
Xiangyu Zhu, Fang Wu, Cheng Zhan, Erjun Kan
Piezocatalysis, which converts mechanical stimuli into chemical energy, holds significant promise for noninvasive medical therapies. In this process, ultrasonic frequency plays a dual role: it governs both the reaction rate and the electromechanical coupling efficiency, thereby serving as a critical bridge between microscopic and macroscopic physical processes. However, conventional theoretical models lack a multiscale description of coupled physical processes and thus fail to reveal how frequency dictates catalytic activity. Here, we develop an integrated multiscale framework that links, for the first time, macroscopic bubble cavitation dynamics, mesoscopic piezoelectric constitutive relations, and microscopic chemical reaction rate─with ultrasonic frequency as the unifying thread. Our model uncovers the complete frequency-dependent activity profile and elucidates the physical origin of an optimal frequency, predicting a volcano-shaped activity-frequency relationship that agrees well with a range of experimental reports. By reinterpreting piezocatalysis from a multiscale physical field perspective, this work establishes a new theoretical paradigm for the rational design of piezocatalysts.

item.title: JACS: Benzaldehyde Is the Redox Mediator for Aerobic C–N Cleavage in Epoxy Composite Recycling
item.description:
Zehan Yu, Ding-Yuan Lim, Andrew R. Rander, Travis J. Williams, Steven R. Nutt
Chemical methods are promising avenues to recycle fiber-reinforced polymer waste. Here, we reintroduce tripotassium phosphate-mediated benzyl alcohol conditions for epoxy cleavage. While these conditions were developed in 2008 for anhydride-cured epoxy cleavage and have been applied to amine-linked epoxy cleavage, no account has been made of why these conditions should work with the latter, or why air exposure appears critical for their success. We now show how benzaldehyde, formed in situ from benzyl alcohol, plays the crucial redox role that enables selective C–N bond cleavage: tertiary amines are cleaved by a previously uncharacterized mechanism in which benzaldehyde facilitates iminium formation from the polymer’s C–N linkage. Subsequent hydrolysis and base-promoted elimination cleave the C═N and C–O bonds, respectively, enabling the recovery of bisphenol A and release of the linking diamines. Carbon fiber (CF) and even glass fiber (GF) fabrics are preserved, and recovered CF fabrics are remanufactured into second-generation composites with near-virgin quality and mechanical performance. These mechanistic insights may inform the future development of selective diamine recovery strategies from thermosets, which is a challenge when valorizing composites. Collectively, these results present promising recycling conditions with the potential to valorize matrices and fibers from a wide range of composites, spanning high-performance carbon fiber to widely used fiberglass.

item.title: JACS: Spin Polarization Enhanced Photocatalytic N2 Reduction on Chiral Mesostructured Bi2WO6
item.description:
Jiamin Ma, Wanning Zhang, Lu Han, Shunai Che, Yuxi Fang
Harnessing the earth-abundant N2 via photocatalysis is a sustainable route to green NH3 synthesis. However, photocatalytic N2 reduction (PNR) remains constrained by the high energy barrier for N2 activation and reduction. In this work, we report that the spin-polarized chiral mesostructured Bi2WO6 (CMB) can facilitate the formation of metastable triplet NOH (3NOH) intermediates, while simultaneously promoting the separation and transport of photogenerated charge carriers, thereby enhancing PNR performance. The CMB was fabricated via a hydrothermal method using tartaric acid as a symmetry-breaking agent. Under sacrificial-agent-free conditions, the NH3 yield of 1325.5 μmol gcat–1 h–1 was achieved, representing a 4.7-fold enhancement over the best values reported for Bi- and W-based catalysts. The pronounced accumulation of the *NOH intermediate, a key precursor to NH3, is speculated to originate from the 3NOH intermediate, driven by the spin polarization of CMB. This work reveals the critical role of spin polarization in regulating triplet reaction intermediates and charge-carrier dynamics during N2 reduction, providing an effective strategy for the design of advanced photocatalysts for sustainable NH3 synthesis.

item.title: ACS Nano: Reconstruction of Oxygen Evolution Precatalysts: Effects of Leaching, Electrolyte Concentration and Iron Incorporation
item.description:
Xinzhang Lin, J. Niklas Hausmann, Na An, Suptish Ghosh, Stefan Mebs, Zhe Xue, Holger Dau, Matthias Driess, et al.
Fe-containing Ni oxyhydroxides are among the most active alkaline oxygen evolution catalysts, whose structures and performances strongly depend on precursor reconstruction and Fe location. However, achieving precise control over precursor design, reconstruction, and Fe incorporation remains highly challenging. Here, we report the low-temperature synthesis of intermetallic Ni2In3 nanoparticles as a precursor and uncover their in situ reconstruction behavior modulated by electrolyte concentration. Compared with similarly sized Ni nanoparticle-derived catalysts, the Ni2In3-derived catalysts exhibit significantly enhanced activity and stability. The optimal catalyst, after activation in 6 M KOH with Fe spiking, requires an overpotential of only 284 mV for 10 mA cm–2, along with a low Tafel slope of 31 mV dec–1. Combined electrochemical analyses, in situ/ex situ characterizations, and theoretical calculations reveal that In leaching induces electronic structure modulation and surface undercoordinated site enrichment, thereby facilitating interfacial Fe incorporation to form NiFe active centers. In an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer, the catalyst demonstrates excellent stability of 260 h at 1 A cm–2 at 80 °C. These findings highlight the importance of electrolyte- and precursor-dependent reconstruction in modulating the electronic structure and promoting interfacial Fe incorporation, thereby enabling the design of oxygen evolution electrocatalysts.

item.title: Nano Letters: Enhanced Electron Charging Induces Positive Aging of QD-LEDs: An Electrically Excited Transient Absorption Study
item.description:
Zhijie Yan, Bo Li, Wenjing Zhang, Yaqi Guo, Leilei Zhao, Qing Xue, Yu Yan, Xingzhi Wang, et al.
Quantum dot light-emitting diodes (QD-LEDs) require encapsulation to extend their storage and operational lifetime. However, acidic encapsulants commonly used usually induce an anomalous positive aging phenomenon─the device performance improves rather than decreases in the initial days. These uncontrollable gains hinder the commercialization of QD-LEDs, yet no study to date has directly probed the in situ evolution of charge carriers during this process. Here, we employ electrically excited transient absorption (EETA) spectroscopy to investigate how encapsulants influence charge carrier dynamics in QD-LEDs. Taking red QD-LEDs as a model system, we demonstrate that positive aging is accompanied by enhanced electron charging in the quantum dot (QD) layer and accelerated electron injection into the emissive layer. Furthermore, we show that acid-induced progressive passivation of surface defects on ZnMgO nanoparticles improves electron injection efficiency. This work reveals that enhanced electron charging induces positive aging in QD-LEDs.

item.title: ACS Nano: Performance of a 5 V-Class Thin-Film Li Battery at a High Current Density of ∼30 mA cm–2
item.description:
Asuka Oi, Kazunori Nishio, Kurei Edamura, Yuki Takeda, Shigeru Kobayashi, Ryo Nakayama, Ryota Shimizu, Taro Hitosugi
All-solid-state Li batteries operating at high current densities exceeding 10 mA cm–2 are desired for high-power and rapid-charging batteries. Therefore, battery development needs to focus on reducing the electrolyte–electrode interface resistance at high current density, which is a major contributor to internal resistance. However, methods for reducing the electrolyte–electrode interfacial resistance at high current densities remain unexplored. Here, we demonstrate charge–discharge operation at 30 mA cm–2 using Li3PS4, LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, and Li metal as a solid electrolyte, 5 V-class positive electrode, and negative electrode, respectively. The introduction of Li3PO4 buffer layers at both Li–Li3PS4 and Li3PS4–LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4 interfaces reduced the interfacial resistance 45,000-fold. Furthermore, the introduction of a 5 nm-thick Pt layer instead of Li3PO4 at the Li–Li3PS4 interface enabled charge–discharge operation under high-current-density conditions. This quantitative study highlights the importance of designing electrochemically robust negative electrode and electrolyte interfaces for high-power 5 V-class all-solid-state Li batteries.

item.title: Nano Letters: Excitation-Wavelength-Dependent Dual Emission in Au42 Quantum Rods
item.description:
Guiying He, Lianshun Luo, Mircea Cotlet, Guoxiang Hu, Gangli Wang, Rongchao Jin
Dual emissive materials are of particular importance in chemical and biological assays. Herein, we focus on a rod-shaped Au42(SCH2CH2Ph)32 nanocluster that exhibits dual emission at 875 and 1040 nm owing to fluorescence (FL) and phosphorescence (PH), respectively. Transient absorption analysis shows a slow intersystem crossing (ISC, ∼500 ps) from lowest singlet S1 to triplet T1 upon direct S1 excitation, leading to dual emission from both S1 and T1. However, upon excitation of the higher Sn state, we observe a metastable singlet state (S′). We rationalize two competing decay pathways from S′: (i) internal conversion to S1 and (ii) ISC to high triplet Tn≥2. These processes alter the populations of the S1 and T1 states, which explains the excitation-wavelength-dependent dual emission and FL/PH ratios. The revealed excited-state mechanism and the dual emissive Au42 material will serve as a paradigm for future research on atomically precise nanoclusters.

item.title: JACS: Solvent-Dipole Deshielding of Hydrated Aluminum Lewis Acids for Enhanced 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural Production from Biomass
item.description:
Huaqing Zhang, Shengkai Cao, Fu Lun Tan, Ya Wen Tay, James Zhile Wong, Haikuo Zhang, Ning-Yu Huang, Jiawei Li, et al.
5-Hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) is a key biomass-derived platform chemical for producing furan-based fuels, fine chemicals, and polymers. Its production from glucose in homogeneous catalytic systems, however, is often limited by the solvation of Lewis acid catalytic centers, where coordinating solvent molecules and anions can shield the active sites, restrict substrate access, and diminish HMF yield and selectivity. Here, we demonstrate that polar aprotic cosolvents can function as active components of the catalytic microenvironment rather than passive reaction media. In water-rich AlCl3 solutions, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), N,N-dimethylacetamide (DMA), and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) exert dipole–dipole interactions with Al-coordinated water molecules through hydrogen bonding, distorting the [Al(H2O)6]3+ solvation shell and increasing access to the Lewis acidic Al center without directly coordinating to it. Spectroscopic measurements and electronic-structure calculations reveal that weakening of the Al–O(water) interaction increases in the order of DMF < DMA < DMSO. This solvation-shell deshielding decreases the apparent activation energy for glucose-to-fructose isomerization from 96 to 79 kJ·mol–1 and enables an HMF yield of 90% from glucose at 150 °C. Glucose streams derived from sugarcane bagasse, poplar sawdust, and palm trunk sawdust afford HMF yields exceeding 80%, while the integrated sugarcane-bagasse route achieves a 49 mol % HMF yield based on the cellulose originally present in the biomass. These results establish dipolar cosolvent control of hydrated metal centers as a molecular design principle for homogeneous biomass conversion.

item.title: Nano Letters: Excitonic Physics in Emerging 2D Semiconductors: A First-Principles Many-Body Perspective from Photodetection to Solar Energy Conversion
item.description:
Michele Re Fiorentin, Simone Grillo, Fulvio Paleari, Olivia Pulci, Daniele Varsano, Maurizia Palummo
Chemically and structurally diverse two-dimensional semiconductors exhibit a broad range of excitonic and optical phenomena that have direct implications for optoelectronic functionality. We examine these materials from a first-principles many-body perspective, emphasizing the connection between microscopic excitonic structure and optoelectronic functionality. Reduced symmetry and orbital character produce polarization-selective absorption, while dimensionality, dielectric screening, and exciton fine structure govern binding energies and radiative behavior. In layered systems, interlayer electrostatics and type-II band alignment promote charge separation, whereas exciton–phonon coupling activates indirect optical transitions and shapes temperature-dependent spectra. These mechanisms establish common design principles for excitonic engineering, whereby the dielectric environment, crystal geometry, lattice dynamics, and stacking are used to control exciton properties and tailor optical functionality. This perspective moves beyond description toward the ab initio prediction and design of emerging 2D materials for targeted optoelectronic applications, including polarization-sensitive photodetection and ultrathin solar-energy conversion.

item.title: JACS: Single-Water Microsolvation Promotes Proton Sharing in a Neutral Formic Acid–Ammonia Complex
item.description:
Fan Xie, Luigi Crisci, Wenhao Sun, Federico Lazzari, Vincenzo Barone, Melanie Schnell
Can single-water microsolvation promote proton sharing in a neutral acid–base complex? We address this question for formic acid–ammonia by isolating its monohydrated complex with broadband rotational spectroscopy and interpreting the resolved 14N hyperfine structure with calibrated high-level quantum chemistry. The observed complex is a single dominant HCOOH–NH3–H2O isomer with effective Cs symmetry, in which NH3 remains the primary proton acceptor, while water closes a cooperative hydrogen-bond cycle by accepting from NH3 and donating to the carbonyl oxygen. Rather than simply stabilizing the binary acid–base contact, this water molecule measurably increases its proton-sharing character. A resolved A/E tunneling pattern from NH3 internal rotation supplies the missing orientation needed to rotate the experimental 14N quadrupole tensor into the local ammonia frame, yielding an experimental χzz component and a quadrupole-derived Townes–Dailey ionicity of approximately 26%. High-level structures show the same directional response: O–H elongation, H···N contraction, and O···N contraction relative to HCOOH–NH3. Together, these results show that one water molecule can promote proton sharing in a neutral formic acid–ammonia complex without producing a separated ion pair.

item.title: Nano Letters: Polymorphic Hf(Zr)O2-Based Films for High-k Dielectrics
item.description:
Beikai Ding, Haoyu Lu, Xuanyu Zhao, Yu Li, Li Zheng, Shiwei Xia, Qi Liu, Hao Jiang, et al.
HfO2/ZrO2-based (HZO) materials are promising high-k dielectrics for integrated capacitors and advanced electronic devices. However, their performance is fundamentally constrained by polymorph competition and the trade-off between the dielectric constant and leakage current. Here, we report a stacking-engineered strategy that integrates HZO layers with optimized ferroelectric and dielectric properties separated by an Al2O3 interlayer (HAZO). A nonswitching pulse measurement is employed to exclude polarization-switching contributions and directly probe the intrinsic dielectric response. The optimized HAZO dielectric exhibits an enhanced dielectric constant while simultaneously suppressing leakage and improving the dielectric breakdown characteristics. Structural characterizations reveal that the engineered stacking stabilizes the coexistence of nonpolar tetragonal and polar orthorhombic phases and increases the phase-boundary density. This polymorphic configuration suppresses irreversible domain switching and enables a stable enhanced dielectric response. These results establish a robust pathway toward high-performance HZO-based dielectrics and provide key insights into tailoring dielectric properties through polymorphic-phase engineering.

item.title: JACS: A Tumor-Activatable DNA Nanoengager That Orchestrates NK Receptor Clustering and Immune Checkpoint Blockage to Enhance Antitumor Cytotoxicity
item.description:
Wen-Jia Shi, Chao-Qiang Li, Wen-Rong Lai, Xiao-Mei Li, Hui-Juan Cheng, Yue Wang, Yang Gao, Pei-Qiang Ma, et al.
Natural killer cell engagers (NKCEs) are promising immunotherapeutic agents for cancer treatment. However, their efficacy against solid tumors is severely limited by immune evasion mechanisms (mediated by the sialic acid–Siglec axis and PD-1/PD-L1 pathway), along with poor pharmacokinetics and off-target effects. Harnessing the precision and addressability of DNA origami, we engineered a tissue-specific, DNA origami-based, dual checkpoint-inhibiting NK synapse engager. This nanoplatform adopts a bilayered barrel architecture: the inner layer is functionalized with aNKp46, aPD-L1, and sialidase, while the outer layer is modified with the serum albumin-binding peptide ABD035 and a pH-sensitive i-motif switch. In the acidic tumor microenvironment, the DNA nanoengager undergoes specific dissociation of the outer protective layer, exposing the functional modules. These components concurrently bridge and activate NK cells, block the PD-L1 immune checkpoint, and specifically degrade tumor surface sialic acids, thereby reversing dual immunosuppression. This integrated DNA system enables synergistic integration of targeted activation, dual checkpoint blockade, and tumor microenvironment responsiveness, providing a novel smart nanoscale strategy to overcome multifaceted immune evasion in solid tumors and enhance the safety and efficacy of NK cell-based immunotherapy.

item.title: ACS Nano: Mode-Selective Tip-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy Reveals Asymmetric Chemical and Carrier-Sensitive Raman Grading in Photovoltaic III–V Tandem Nanowire Junctions
item.description:
Vanessa Hinojosa-Chasiquiza, Jose Luis Pura, Siiri Bienz, Yue Zhao, Jordi Antoja-Lleonart, Magnus Borgström, Francesc Pérez-Murano, Sergio Muñoz de Baena, et al.
Performance of tandem junction nanowire (NW) solar cells relies on the electronic quality of the tunnel diodes which serve as the separating junctions between subcells. Yet, the relevant interfacial physics occurs below the optical diffraction limit. Here we use hyperspectral tip-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (TERS) to map, with nanoscale precision, axially defined heterojunctions in InP/InGaP tandem junction photovoltaic NWs. By resolving mode-specific phonon and phonon–plasmon responses, we show that the nominally abrupt p/p++ and p++/n++ junctions are compositionally graded. The TOM mode, used as the primary compositional marker, yields transition widths of ∼90–120 nm, whereas other lattice- and carrier-sensitive modes exhibit broader central widths up to ∼190 nm, reflecting their additional sensitivity to alloying, structural disorder, and electronic coupling. In a first-order approximation, rescaling these TERS-derived widths to shorter, device-relevant NWs yields narrower junctions, consistent with independent Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) measurements that qualitatively capture the same trend despite surface and tip convolution effects. Complementary equilibrium band-edge model combined with a simplified one-dimensional Wentzel–Kramers–Brillouin (WKB) calculation, as an illustrative trend, further indicates that such grading is expected to widen the effective tunnel barrier. These findings establish mode-selective hyperspectral TERS as a validated, noninvasive method for quantitative nanoscale mapping of compositional grading in III–V NW junctions, with the carrier-sensitive L1 phonon–plasmon response providing complementary, model-assisted insight into the electronic evolution of the junctions.

item.title: Nano Letters: Optically Active Single Hole Spin in ZnSe
item.description:
Amirehsan Alizadehherfati, Yuxi Jiang, Kelsey J. Mirrielees, Nils von den Driesch, Christine Falter, Yurii Kutovyi, Amirehsan Boreiri, Douglas L. Irving, et al.
Semiconductor hole spins offer a pathway to extended coherence times by decoupling from nuclear magnetic noise, while their spin–orbit coupling enables fast all-electrical control. In ZnSe, however, realizing this potential has been limited by p-doping challenges. Here, we circumvent this limit by optically activating acceptors and demonstrate optical spin initialization. We isolate a single-hole spin bound to a shallow acceptor, confirmed by antibunching and accessed via the fast (244 ps) radiative recombination of a bound exciton. Magnetic and Raman spectroscopy reveal a spin-selective Λ system with an effective hole g-factor of 0.7 and an optical line width of 26.7 GHz. Time-resolved measurements reveal optical pumping of the hole spin with an estimated initialization fidelity of 90.7%. First-principles simulations combined with the experiment identify nitrogen as the most likely acceptor impurity. These results introduce a promising new platform for optically active spin qubits and single-photon sources in ZnSe.

item.title: JACS: Stabilization and Transformation of MXenes into Flexible and Thermal Oxidation-Resistant Non-van der Waals solids via Vapor-Phase Chemical Intercalation
item.description:
Qi Zhao, Peng Yi, Zongju Cheng, Riming Hu, Xinping Wu, Zhiguo Du, Shubin Yang
Non-van der Waals (non-vdW) solids derived from MXenes exhibit attractive physical and chemical properties but are usually limited by the irreversible phase transformation of MXenes into rocksalt structures at high temperatures. Herein, we develop a vapor-phase chemical intercalation strategy mediated by high-vapor-pressure zinc (Zn) to efficiently stabilize the transition metals (Ti, Nb, and V) with unsaturated d-orbitals in MXenes. This stabilization facilitates subsequent interlayer bonding via reaction with various metal vapors (Al, Ga, and In) at elevated temperatures, yielding a family of well-defined non-vdW solids with ultrathin layered structures. Moreover, this strategy is readily scalable, enabling the fabrication of a continuous non-vdW Al–Ti3C2 film featuring a heterogeneous architecture with a reconstructed MAX-like bonded region and a locally unbonded MXene region. These structural features endow the non-vdW Al–Ti3C2 film with exceptional mechanical flexibility, high-temperature oxidation resistance at 800 °C in air, and an electrical conductivity of ∼10 000 S cm–1. Consequently, the film demonstrates an electromagnetic interference shielding effectiveness of up to 47.9 dB at a thickness of 5 μm, along with durable infrared stealth performance under prolonged exposure at 500 °C for 48 h.

item.title: JACS: Tailored ZnO/Cellulose Separator Reconfigures Solvation Chemistry for Durable Magnesium Metal Batteries
item.description:
Shuai Guo, Yi Yang, Siwen Lu, Aobing Du, Longfei Wen, Guochuan Tang, Xiaoniu Guo, Enhui Wang, et al.
Magnesium metal batteries represent highly promising candidates for sustainable energy storage owing to their extremely high volumetric capacity (3833 mAh cm–3), abundant raw materials, and intrinsic safety. However, their practical viability is severely impeded by uneven Mg deposition, catastrophic interfacial side reactions, and continuous gassing behavior driven by uncontrolled electrolyte decomposition. Herein, we first report an inorganic inter-reinforced organic composite separator, fabricated by pairing cellulose with a zinc oxide (ZnO)-enhanced layer and designed to regulate the electrolyte solvation architecture by effectively anchoring solvent molecules. Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses reveal that the electron-deficient Zn sites on ZnO enhance the solvent-capture ability of the polar hydroxyl groups on cellulose via bidirectional charge transfer. This interaction reconfigures the Mg2+ solvation sheath into a unique single-cluster structure, steering the formation of a dense, ultrathin, inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) that facilitates rapid Mg2+ desolvation while suppressing parasitic side reactions. Consequently, the as-assembled Mg||Mg symmetric cells deliver an exceptional cycling lifespan exceeding 2000 h with minimal overpotential and exhibit robust compatibility across diverse electrolyte systems. This inorganic inter-reinforced organic strategy for modulating solvation chemistry offers a generalizable avenue toward long-life and high-safety magnesium metal batteries.

item.title: Nano Letters: Interface-Induced Crystallographic Orientation of Zinc Deposition Enabled by a Zwitterionic Dynamic Buffering Interface for Ultralong-Life Aqueous Zinc Batteries
item.description:
Xin Wei, Qing-Yuan Zhao, Ji-Zun Zhang, Hai Xu, Zi-Yan Liu, Naoyuki Shibayama, Yu-Ting Xu, Xiao-Feng Wang
The development of aqueous zinc batteries is critically constrained by the electrode–electrolyte interfacial instability at the Zn anode. Herein, a zwitterionic dynamic buffering interface (ZDBI) is constructed by using trace glufosinate ammonium (GA). The dissociated GA– anchors onto the Zn(101) surface via its phosphinate and carboxylate groups with its protonated amino group (−NH3+) extending into the electrolyte to dynamically respond to interfacial electric fields. Meanwhile, free NH4+ cations can form an electrostatic shielding layer under an electric field. This synergistic chemisorbed-mobile-ion buffering network thickens the electric double layer, inhibits water-splitting parasitic reactions, and induces (101)-oriented deposition. Consequently, Zn||Zn symmetric cells sustain stable cycling for over 7800 h with a cumulative capacity of 3.9 Ah cm–2, while Zn||Cu half-cells achieve an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.3%, and Zn||V2O5 full cells retain 88% capacity after 1000 cycles at 5 A g–1. This work offers an efficient strategy for addressing electrode–electrolyte interfacial issues.

item.title: Nano Letters: Dynamics of Charge-Density-Wave Puddles in 2 H -NbSe2
item.description:
Shreya Kumbhakar, Marina Esposito, Anjan Kumar N M, Liwen Feng, Tommaso Confalone, Vasilisa Gerega, Flavia Lo Sardo, Rafiqul Alam, et al.
Electronic phases in quantum materials are often governed by nanoscale inhomogeneity, where local order develops within spatially confined regions, or puddles. A prominent example is an incommensurate charge-density-wave (I-CDW) comprising locally commensurate domains. In 2H-NbSe2, such an I-CDW state persists alongside lattice anharmonicity and superconductivity, raising fundamental questions about the dynamical stabilization of CDW order in puddles. Here, using Raman scattering, we reveal a strong Fano-coupling between interlayer shear phonons and the CDW amplitude mode. Our time-resolved reflectivity measurement shows a low-frequency ∼0.2 THz coherent overdamped oscillation onsetting within the CDW regime at ∼17K, indicating a previously unexplored transition. This we identify as a Fano-coupled phonon-CDW hybrid emerging from the collective dynamics of CDW puddles. We establish an overdamped-oscillator framework for capturing such intertwined glassy dynamics. These results highlight how lattice pinning and electronic correlations shape CDW order in layered materials, insight crucial for designing novel van der Waals devices.

item.title: Nano Letters: Natural Hyperbolic Dispersion in Anisotropic Bulk and Nanoscaled Copper Chalcogenides
item.description:
Urvi Parekh, Achyut Tiwari, Bruno Gompf, Nadiia Didukh, Jivesh Kaushal, Stefan Scheel, Christian Klinke, Rostyslav Lesyuk
Hyperbolic media support high-k electromagnetic modes, enabling subdiffractional confinement, anomalous refraction, and enhanced light–matter interactions. While most hyperbolic metamaterials rely on artificial structuring, natural hyperbolicity arises from crystal anisotropy and direction-dependent plasma frequencies. Here we provide direct experimental evidence for natural hyperbolicity in copper chalcogenides by spectroscopic ellipsometry in the visible–near-infrared range. We demonstrate hyperbolic dispersion in bulk covellite CuS by identifying a spectral window where the real parts of the in-plane and out-of-plane permittivity components have opposite signs. The study is then expanded to size-controlled CuS nanosheets as oriented films. Using the Bruggeman effective medium approximation to account for the nanostructure/void composite, we show that hyperbolicity persists upon nanoscaling and that the epsilon-near-zero condition and hyperbolic bandwidth shift with size. Finally, we demonstrate analogous behavior in klockmannite CuSe nanosheets, establishing copper chalcogenides as a tunable platform for natural hyperbolicity at the boundary of the NIR and visible ranges.

item.title: ACS Nano: Capturing Transient Intermediate Assembly States Enables Hierarchical Core–Shell Microassemblies with Spatiotemporal Release for Psoriasis Therapy
item.description:
Duohang Bi, Rui Geng, Soyoung Son, Yanlin Wang, Yilin Liao, Yufeng Sun, Ziqiang Xu, Hongyao Du, et al.
Coordinated delivery of therapeutics with distinct physicochemical properties remains a fundamental challenge in drug design. This difficulty often stems from incompatible assembly kinetics, in which mismatched assembly behaviors among components lead to disordered structures and hinder functional integration. Here, we report a cascade assembly strategy to construct core–shell microassemblies (MTX@HPTD) by capturing transient intermediate states, enabling sequential structural organization and functional integration for spatiotemporal drug release. Upon solvent exchange, methotrexate (MTX) and phenylboronic acid-modified hyaluronic acid (HP) coassemble, thereby allowing the capture of an intermediate in which a dense MTX-rich core forms while the surrounding HP shell remains accessible for subsequent integration. This enables covalent anchoring of ROS-scavenging TEMPO-doped polydopamine nanoparticles (TPDA) into the evolving shell of the intermediate assembly via dynamic covalent bonding. The resulting core–shell microassemblies, featuring an MTX-rich reservoir stabilized by a functionalized HP-rich shell that entraps the TPDA payload, exhibit spatially segregated compartments, enabling diffusion-controlled release of MTX and stimuli-responsive release of TPDA. Moreover, by utilizing changes in the size of microassemblies during release, this system addresses the size-dependent trade-off between retention and uptake. In a psoriasis model, microneedle-mediated delivery achieves coordinated therapy, suppressing ferroptosis, necroptosis, and HMGB1 signaling, thereby mitigating disease severity. This work establishes the temporal capture of transient states as a promising strategy for constructing hierarchical materials for spatiotemporal release.

item.title: Nano Letters: Dimensional Engineering of Co/W Superlattices Enables Out-of-Plane Spin Polarization with 90% Field-Free Switching in Perpendicular CoFeB
item.description:
Yu-Lon Lin, Jing-Wen Chen, Yan-Zhen Huang, Tzu-Chuan Hsin, Chih-Wei Cheng, Yu-Han Huang, Ssu-Yen Huang, Shintaro Hara, et al.
Deterministic spin–orbit torque (SOT) switching of perpendicular magnets without external magnetic fields remains a central challenge for scalable SOT-MRAM. Here, we demonstrate that dimensional engineering of a Co/W superlattice spin–orbit layer enables >90% field-free switching of perpendicular CoFeB. Harmonic Hall measurements reveal an unconventional out-of-plane torque, while first-principles calculations reveal reconstruction of the spin-resolved electronic structure and increased W-projected out-of-plane spin character, together supporting the modification of torque symmetry through Co/W superlattice engineering. The optimized superlattice achieves a critical current density of 23.3 MA cm–2 and a thermal stability factor Δ ≈ 45. Nanoscale devices (100 nm) preserve deterministic field-free reversal with comparable efficiency, confirming scalability toward magnetic tunnel junction integration. Micromagnetic analysis shows that out-of-plane spin-polarized torque together with canted anisotropy enables intrinsic symmetry breaking, highlighting superlattice engineering as a route to tailor torque symmetry for effective field-free SOT devices.

item.title: JACS: In Situ Ion-Exchange-Mediated Dynamic Nanointerface Reconfiguration for Polarity-Switchable Photoelectrochemical–Photothermal Biosensing
item.description:
Hao Cheng, Zhen Yang, Dan Yang, Chuanping Li, Ren Cai, Weihong Tan
Conventional photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems typically rely on static semiconductor interfaces that merely translate biomolecular recognition into amplitude modulation of the pre-existing photocurrent, thus limiting their analytical robustness and self-validation capabilities. Herein, we report in situ ion-exchange-mediated dynamic nanointerface engineering to fabricate an analyte-programmed reconfigurable PEC–photothermal (PT) dual-mode biosensor for the carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) assay. The Z-scheme heterostructure of a plasmonic Au nanoparticle (NP) layer-supported BiOI/AgI/indium tin oxide glass (BiOI/AgI/Au NPs/ITO) is constructed as the initial photoelectrode. In the sensing process, a CEA recognition event directly reshapes the phase composition of BiOI/AgI, charge-transfer behavior, and photoresponse polarity. The synergistic integration of the BiOI/AgI heterostructure and the close-packed layer of plasmonic Au NPs substantially enhance the light absorption, charge separation, and interfacial charge transfer, making BiOI/AgI/Au NPs/ITO a highly suitable photoelectrode for the PEC mode of the PEC–PT biosensor. This analyte-driven phase evolution reconstructs the semiconductor composition, band alignment, and charge-transfer pathways to switch the photocurrent polarity from cathodic to anodic. In addition, a photothermal imaging mode of the PEC–PT biosensor is triggered by regulating the Bi2S3 formation for intrinsic cross-validation. By integrating an artificial neural network (ANN)-assisted analysis, PEC–PT biosensors enable robust multimodal quantification and improved analytical reliability, achieving > 99.8% prediction accuracy in real-sample analysis. This is the first example of integrating a dynamic nanointerface-driven PEC–PT dual-mode biosensor with artificial intelligence (AI)-enhanced multimodal analysis for CEA detection and provides a dynamic nanointerface-driven strategy for intelligent multimode biosensing.

item.title: JACS: Three-Dimensional Covalent Organic Framework for the Capture of Nitrogen Dioxide
item.description:
Thien D. Duong, Siyu Zhou, Xin Lian, Zhaozhao Hu, Yuhang Yang, Zi Wang, Ran Eitan Abutbul, Joseph Hurd, et al.
We report the first adsorption isotherm of nitrogen dioxide (NO2) in covalent organic frameworks (COFs). Leveraging the dihedral angle (43.6°) of the biphenyl unit in biphenyl-3,3′,5,5′-tetracarbaldehyde, upon reaction with p-phenylenediamine, a three-dimensional COF, PKU-800, has been synthesized. Powder X-ray diffraction, hyperpolarised solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and modeling collectively reveal that PKU-800 exhibits a triply interpenetrated qtz-type framework structure, which incorporates missing-aldehyde defects (∼8%) and thus pendant amine termini (∼16%). At 298 K, PKU-800 shows remarkable adsorption of NO2 (4.8 and 18.8 mmol g–1 at 0.01 and 1.0 bar, respectively), representing a new benchmark for NO2 sorbents. Dynamic breakthrough experiments confirm efficient capture of NO2 (from 2500 to < 0.1 ppm) by PKU-800 under both dry and wet conditions, with dynamic capacities of 4.97 and 5.27 mmol g–1, respectively. In situ spectroscopic and modeling studies reveal that PKU-800 combines a robust three-dimensional topology, fully accessible channels, and strong binding interactions at both the imine and amino sites to synergistically trap NO2, which can be converted readily to nitric acid upon reaction with water in air.

item.title: ACS Nano: Decoupled Channel and Contact Modulation in α-In2Se3/ZrO2/Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 Dual-Ferroelectric Field-Effect Transistor
item.description:
Jee Hwan Lee, Jung Um Park, Won Woo Lee, Whan Kyun Kim, Do Kyeong Yun, Minh Chien Nguyen, Yoon Seon An, Huamin Li, et al.
Ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) utilizing either a ferroelectric dielectric (FeD) or a ferroelectric semiconductor (FeS) are highly promising for neuromorphic computing. While integrating FeD with emerging FeS could provide new degrees of freedom for synaptic plasticity, direct integration inevitably suffers from unintended electrostatic coupling and a lack of independent polarization control. Here, we demonstrate a structurally decoupled dual-ferroelectric field-effect transistor (Dual-FeFET) based on an α-In2Se3/ZrO2/HZO heterostructure, in which a ferroelectric dielectric and a ferroelectric semiconductor are integrated into a single transistor while retaining independent functional roles. The inserted ZrO2 interfacial layer mitigates unintended polarization coupling between HZO and α-In2Se3, enabling two orthogonal memory operations: gate-bias-induced HZO polarization switching globally modulates the carrier density of the α-In2Se3 channel, whereas drain-bias-induced α-In2Se3 polarization switching predominantly modulates the drain-side Schottky barrier near the contact region. Dual-mode PFM, Hall-bar analysis, temperature-dependent transport measurements, and ZrO2-thickness-dependent control experiments support the largely decoupled modulation of channel transport and contact injection. By sequentially exploiting these two modulation modes, the Dual-FeFET extends the conductance dynamic range and improves the linearity of synaptic potentiation compared with conventional single-mode FeFET operation. The device exhibits robust nonvolatile memory characteristics with stable endurance over 105 cycles and retention up to 105 s. When implemented in convolutional neural network simulations for CIFAR-10 image recognition, the Dual-FeFET-based synapses achieve an accuracy of 89.2%, approaching the ideal software accuracy of 96.5% and outperforming conventional single-FeFET-based synapses (74.1%). These results demonstrate that structural ferroelectric decoupling enables independently programmable channel and contact modulation in multifunctional 2D ferroelectric transistors.

item.title: ACS Nano: Marine-Inspired Synergistic Adhesion Enables Highly Efficient and Atraumatic Macromolecular Transdermal Delivery on Dynamic Skin
item.description:
Minwoo Song, Minjin Kim, Jihun Son, Gui Won Hwang, Gyun Ro Kang, Changrok Park, Hyoung-Ki Park, Keun Ho Lee, et al.
Effective transdermal drug delivery (TDD) demands both the ability to bypass the stratum corneum (ST) and the robustness to sustain delivery efficiency under real-life conditions. Despite advances in nanocarriers, microneedles, and electrostimulation, many TDDS strategies face limitations due to cytotoxicity, invasiveness, device dependence, and poor performance for large molecules in real-world conditions. In this study, we present a marine-inspired TDDS patch (PDA@SC) that integrates adhesion strategies from marine organisms to achieve stable skin attachment and atraumatic macromolecular delivery, even on dynamic skin surfaces. The suction-cup (SC) structure, inspired by octopus’ suckers, generates negative pressure upon preload-induced deformation, promoting temporary mechanical modulation for nanolevel control of the ST barrier and enhancing drug delivery without external power. Simultaneously, the mussel-inspired polydopamine (PDA) coating modifies hydrophobic surfaces into high surface energy interfaces capable of chemical bonding, thereby ensuring intimate adhesion and minimizing drug leakage. Experimental findings confirmed that the delivery of the high molecular weight compound was enhanced on deformed skin, showing a 600% improvement compared to conventional topical application. In addition, preliminary human evaluation demonstrated that PDA@SC effectively improved key dermatological parameters. Collectively, these results highlight the potential of PDA@SC as a platform that can drive technological progress in wearable therapeutics and cosmetics.

item.title: JACS: An Atomic-Scale Chemical Switch for Oxide Ferroelectricity
item.description:
Junjie Ding, Wenjun Lv, Wenjun Cui, Zaichun Sun, Yongqiang Li, Wen Zhao, Yunlong Tang, Gustaaf Van Tendeloo, et al.
Interfacial chemistry offers new opportunities for designing ferroelectric materials, yet their coupling with intrinsic polarization remains largely unexplored. Here, we synthesize ferroelectric BiFeO3 nanoparticles with {100} facets covered by a Bi2FeO6-x Aurivillius-like phase, allowing the interfacial Bi2O2 layer to interact with bulk polarization at different relative orientations. Using atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy, we observed a large polarization enhancement when the interface aligned with the bulk polarization, and a polarization reversal when opposing it. In situ heating and first-principles calculations show that the Bi2O2 layer repels the underlying FeO6 octahedra, which either rotate or rigidly displace to accommodate the chemical stress, depending on local geometry. Moreover, this mechanism can imprint local polarization in Aurivillius phases and nonferroelectric oxides, offering a general route to design polar topologies in oxide heterostructures.

item.title: ACS Nano: Triple-Encoding Platform for Multiplexed In Situ Profiling of Extracellular Vesicle miRNAs Enables Precision Diagnosis of Ovarian Cancer
item.description:
Haimeng Pei, Tingzhi Kuang, Yuting Dai, Jin Li, Liyan Zheng, Qingqing Tan, Fengli Qu
Ovarian cancer, the most lethal gynecologic malignancy, urgently demands early and accurate diagnostic methods. Tumor-derived extracellular vesicles (tEVs) hold great promise as noninvasive biomarkers, yet their clinical translation is severely hampered by inherent heterogeneity and the inability of conventional assays to detect multiple types of biomarkers. To break this bottleneck, we developed a novel one-pot, triple-encoding platform that integrates size–fluorescence-encoded beads with a membrane fusion strategy. This enables simultaneous in situ profiling of 11 miRNAs across three distinct EV subpopulations defined by EpCAM/PD-L1 expression. Leveraging machine learning, an 11-miRNA logistic panel achieved tumor versus health discrimination (AUC = 0.995), and a combinatorial signature based on EV subpopulations and miRNA profiles enabled the classification of ovarian cancer subtypes, achieving 78.6% accuracy in the validation cohort. Our work provides a versatile and scalable approach for multiparameter EV analysis, enabling comprehensive EV miRNA profiling and ovarian cancer classification.

item.title: JACS: Wavelength-Selective Magneto-Optical Diodes Based on Rare-Earth Chiral Molecular Crystals
item.description:
Inkarat Atirojwanich, Maxime Aragon-Alberti, Langit Cahya Adi, Kevin Paillot, Mathieu Gascoin, Grégoire David, Boris Le Guennic, Geert L. J. A. Rikken, et al.
Chiral materials, integrating structural breaking of mirror-symmetry, exhibit physical properties that cannot be observed in centrosymmetric analogues. Among these properties, optical magneto-chiral anisotropy, the nonreciprocal absorption of light shown by chiral magnetized systems, is emerging as an enabling technology in magneto-optics and photonics. Here, we report on enantiopure chiral molecular crystals based on the erbium(III) rare-earth ion that display nonreciprocal, wavelength-selective, magnetic field-induced variations of the optical absorption coefficients up to ca. 200% for the intrashell f–f electronic transition falling in the 1.5 μm telecom wavelength range. Such a response is associated with an exceptionally high Magneto-Chiral Dichroism induced by the strong spin–orbit coupling of the Er(III) and the helical chirality at the lanthanide center, exalted by the magnetic-dipole-allowed character of the electronic transition. This chirality-induced nonreciprocal magneto-optical response represents a proof of concept for the use of these chiral crystalline molecular materials as potential components in magneto-optical diodes.

item.title: JACS: Engineering a Reconfigurable Transmembrane Receptor Enables Logic-Controlled Signal Translocation
item.description:
Hui Chen, Liu-Pan Yang, Zhen Zou, Jin Huang, Jing Zheng, Kemin Wang, Jianbo Liu
Transmembrane receptors relay extracellular cues into intracellular responses through reconfigurable conformational changes, yet engineering synthetic systems that emulate receptor-like signal translocation with programmable control remains challenging. Here, we engineer a reconfigurable transmembrane receptor that enables logic-controlled signal translocation across lipid membranes. The receptor is constructed from an oriented Y-shaped triplex DNA architecture that inserts directionally into the plasma membrane via dual cholesterol anchors and integrates two environmental inputs─H+ and ATP─through an i-motif and an aptamer module. Under dual-input conditions, cooperative duplex-to-triplex switching triggers reconfigurable structural rearrangement and drives transmembrane relocation of a signaling strand from the outer to the inner membrane leaflet. This receptor-mediated signal translocation converts extracellular chemical cues into spatially defined intracellular activation. The repositioned strand serves as a modular intracellular effector that can be functionalized to implement programmable reactions, including bioorthogonal catalysis and light-triggered photocatalysis at the membrane interface. Importantly, endogenous tumor-microenvironmental cues trigger receptor reconfiguration and signal translocation in 3D tumor spheroids and in vivo, enabling logic-gated intracellular photocatalysis and >85% tumor growth inhibition in xenograft models. By coupling logic-gated reconfigurable switching with directional transmembrane signal propagation, this work establishes an engineered transmembrane receptor for programmable intracellular activation and provides a general strategy for synthetic signal translocation in living systems.

item.title: Nano Letters: Continuously Tunable Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance of Anisotropic Gold Nanopolyhedrons for Multiplexed Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Imaging
item.description:
Chaoqin He, Xiuwen Zheng, Jingzhi Zhou, Ruo Yuan, Ying Zhuo, Xia Yang
Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is attractive for multiplex bioimaging owing to its excellent photostability and ultranarrow spectral bandwidth. However, achieving synergistic enhancement of excitation and Raman scattering fields remains challenging. Herein, the relationship between geometry and localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) was investigated by continuously tuning the aspect ratio (AR) of anisotropic Au nanopolyhedrons (Au NPHs). Central-body modulation while preserving sharp terminal tips enables continuous LSPR tuning while retaining tip-associated electromagnetic enhancement. The SERS behavior was further analyzed by considering the spectral matching between the LSPR and the excitation/scattering wavelengths. For different excitation wavelengths, the optimal SERS response can be achieved by selecting Au NPHs whose LSPR band best matches with the excitation and Raman scattering wavelengths. These results demonstrate that Raman enhancement is governed by spectral matching rather than a fixed optimal geometry. The optimized Au NPHs enabled the use of dual SERS probes for proof-of-concept multiplex biomarker imaging.

item.title: Nano Letters: Probing Valence Electron Distributions at Subatomic Resolution in a Charge Density Wave Material
item.description:
Anya S. Mulligan, Guomin Zhu, Ece Genc, Eric Cui, Stephen D. Wilson, Susanne Stemmer
Probing the internal electronic structure of complex materials with atomic spatial resolution has remained an outstanding challenge in condensed-matter science. A promising approach is convergent-beam electron diffraction (CBED) in four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM). Here, we apply 4D-STEM CBED to the charge-density-wave (CDW) material 1T-TaS2. We demonstrate a qualitative breakdown of the conventional independent atom model (IAM) in reproducing the experimental CBED patterns. A robust low-angle intensity maximum is systematically absent in IAM-based simulations but is consistently reproduced in simulations that use electrostatic potentials derived from density functional theory. A comparison of CBED patterns with projected charge densities reveals a remarkable correspondence between the local real-space valence charge distribution and diffracted intensities, reflecting site-dependent charge density variations within the CDW structure. These results establish atomic-resolution CBED as an experimental probe of valence electron contributions to the scattering potential and open a route to resolving complex electronic ordering phenomena.

item.title: Nano Letters: Experimental Signature of Transient Symmetry Breaking in a Cavity Dirty-Limit Superconductor
item.description:
Siyu Duan, Jingbo Wu, Xiaoqing Jia, Hongkai Shi, Haojie Li, Anneke Reinold, Huabing Wang, Ilya M. Eremin, et al.
Transient states of matter far from equilibrium may exhibit physical properties beyond those allowed by the equilibrium-state crystalline symmetries. We explore ultrafast and direct electronic excitations of transient states in a dirty-limit superconductor with time-resolved terahertz-pump terahertz-probe spectroscopy. By embedding the superconductor into a designed microcavity structure of metallic split-ring resonators, we can sensitively probe the pump field-induced transient variations of the superconducting states around the cavity’s resonant frequency. Our results show that the strong terahertz field can transiently modify the symmetries of the electronic subsystems via the injection of a picosecond supercurrent, leading to high-order nonlinear dynamical responses that are not compatible with the equilibrium-state symmetries, which is evidence for transient symmetry breaking on the picosecond time scale.

item.title: Nano Letters: Competing Magnetic Configurations Enable Low-Field Magnetoresistance Switching in Cr3Te4
item.description:
Qian Chen, Wei Jiang, Jiaqi Bai, Kaidi Guo, Xingze Dai, Dezheng Yang, Xiaoqian Zhang, Liang He, et al.
Large magnetoresistance typically emerges from transitions between distinct electronic phases or magnetic configurations, yet controllable switching between competing magnetic configurations within a single metallic material remains challenging. Here we investigate magnetotransport in Cr3Te4 and demonstrate a magnetic-field-switchable resistance modulation of up to −37.6%, enabled by the near degeneracy between antiparallel and parallel magnetic configurations. Remarkably, a magnetic field of ∼0.25 T suffices to induce switching between these competing magnetic configurations, accompanied by a reconstruction in electronic transport supported by Boltzmann transport calculations. Substituting 5% of Cr with Co suppresses the switching behavior, consistent with a suppression of the competition between the nearly degenerate magnetic configurations, while the magnetoresistance evolves into a negative longitudinal magnetoresistance, suggesting a possible Weyl-band-related contribution associated with a Co-induced upward shift of the Fermi level. Our results establish competing magnetic configurations as an effective route toward large magnetoresistance in structurally simple metallic systems.

item.title: ACS Nano: Oncolytic Virus-like Nanoparticle Targets the Golgi Apparatus via Sphingomyelin
item.description:
Liming He, Ling Yang, Min Ren, Jie Wang, Wei Zhao, Chunli Yang, Chunyan Pan, Yunkun Xing, et al.
The Golgi apparatus (GA) has emerged as a promising target for cancer therapy. Commonly, therapeutics are guided to the GA by recognizing specific receptors on the GA membrane. However, the low and heterogeneous expression of these receptors often results in suboptimal targeting efficiency. Here, we present an oncolytic virus-like nanoparticle for GA targeting by exploiting sphingomyelin, an abundant component of the GA membrane. This nanoparticle consisted of a polymeric nanocarrier complexed with a plasmid encoding the secreting peptide-deleted α-hemolysin (αHL), a pore-forming protein with high affinity for sphingomyelin. The nanoparticle could transfect cancer cells to induce intracellular expression of αHL, enabling GA targeting through binding to GA-associated sphingomyelin while bypassing the cell membrane. Consequently, the transfected cells exhibited GA structural disassembly and underwent a pyroptosis-like programmed cell death with immunogenic characteristics. Notably, αHL-rich microvesicles were subsequently secreted, effectively killing neighboring tumor cells. Intratumoral administration of this formulation significantly suppressed subcutaneous tumor growth and elicited robust antitumor immunity, preventing tumor rechallenge. Furthermore, by incorporating iRGD-modified polymers, we constructed a tumor-targeting oncolytic virus-like nanoparticle with neutral surface charge. Following intravenous administration, this iRGD-modified nanoparticle could efficiently suppress tumor growth without causing obvious systemic toxicity. Collectively, this work presents a robust strategy for GA-targeting via sphingomyelin recognition, providing a potential approach for GA-targeted anticancer therapeutics.

item.title: ACS Nano: pH-Programmed Poly(amino acid) Nanoparticles for Mucus-Penetrating and Bacteria-Targeted Eradication of Helicobacter pylori
item.description:
Yizhen You, Yuhang Zhou, Runyu Han, Dongdong Zhao, Zibo Yin, Jiazhen Niu, Qing Ni, Liwen Li, et al.
The global prevalence of Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection stands in stark contrast to the limited clinical efficacy of antibiotics, primarily attributed to their rapid inactivation under gastric acidity and poor penetration through the gastric mucus barrier. Here, we report a pH-programmed poly(amino acid)-based nanoplatform for the precise eradication of H. pylori. This platform is constructed from poly(amino acid) block copolymers (FAR) incorporating d-aminoalanine side chains and rhamnolipid (RHL) moieties, which self-assemble into amoxicillin-loaded nanoparticles (Am@FAR NPs). Under strongly acidic gastric conditions (pH < 3), Am@FAR NPs undergo extensive protonation, adopting a compact, stabilized configuration that suppresses premature drug release and preserves antibiotic activity. Upon entering the gastric mucus layer (pH ∼ 4–6), partial deprotonation induces surface charge reversal, reducing nonspecific mucin adhesion and facilitating efficient mucus penetration. Cooperative recognition, mediated by RHL and d-aminoalanine residues, enables selective targeting of H. pylori within the mucus niche; here, further local pH elevation (∼6–7) triggers particle swelling and on-site drug release. Consequently, Am@FAR NPs achieve 99.99% eradication efficiency against H. pyloriin vivo, offering a highly effective and biocompatible strategy for the treatment of gastric H. pylori infections.

item.title: ACS Nano: Membrane-Anchored Dual-Targeting Aptamer Engagers for Programmable T Cell Redirection in Solid and Hematological Cancers
item.description:
Chi Zhang, Si-Yu Zhou, Shu-Qi Wang, Heqing Yi, Yuntian Zhu, Xue-Qiang Wang
Inefficient immune synapse formation limits the therapeutic efficacy of T cell-based immunotherapy in both solid tumors and hematological malignancies. Here, we report a fully synthetic, membrane-anchored dual-targeting aptamer engager, AptE 2, that acts as a programmable artificial immunological interface to redirect cytotoxic T cells toward cancer cells without genetic engineering. Constructed entirely from DNA aptamers through optimized bioorthogonal conjugation and enzyme-mediated ligation, AptE 2 integrates multivalent tumor recognition, T cell binding, enhanced nuclease resistance, and prolonged membrane anchoring within a single modular scaffold. In colorectal cancer models, AptE 2 promoted stable T cell–tumor cell engagement, enhanced cytotoxicity and cytokine secretion, and drove pronounced tumor regression with increased intratumoral CD8+ T cell infiltration and minimal systemic toxicity. Importantly, AptE 2 also demonstrated broad applicability in leukemia. In CCRF-CEM cells, AptE 2 exhibited strong surface binding, sustained membrane retention for up to 6 h, and superior resistance to wash-off compared with monovalent aptamers and bivalent controls. AptE 2-prearmed TALL-104 cells markedly enhanced leukemia cell clustering, increased cell lysis to over 90% under optimized coculture conditions, and amplified IFN-γ secretion. In a disseminated CCRF-CEM-Luc leukemia mouse model, AptE 2-mediated T cell therapy suppressed systemic leukemia progression, improved peripheral hematological profiles, and showed favorable tolerability without detectable major organ injury. These findings establish AptE 2 as a generalizable, nonprotein-based and nonviral immune engager platform for programmable T cell redirection across both solid and hematological cancers.

item.title: JACS: Metal Fluorides: All-In-One Supports for Ruthenium-Catalyzed Ammonia Synthesis
item.description:
Xiaohu Hu, Yifan Yan, Jiakai Wang, Haolong Chang, Zhongliang Cao, Yanru Wang, Haoran Qian, Xiaorou Cao, et al.
Ammonia, an emerging energy carrier, demands advanced catalysts for synthesis under mild conditions to integrate with green hydrogen. We herein establish a family of metal fluoride supports (MFn, M = Li, Na, K, Mg, Ca, or Ba) as a tunable “all-in-one” platform for ruthenium (Ru) catalysts. These Ru/MFn systems unify the critical merits of various existing catalysts, such as support-mediated activation of reactants and air stability. Varying the host cation can direct the catalytic pathway. Consequently, Ru/NaF exhibits excellent turnover frequency, while Ru/BaF2 delivers an NH3 synthesis rate of 58.0 mmolNH3 gcat–1 h–1 at 400 °C and 0.9 MPa─surpassing all reported Ru-based catalysts with ≤4 wt % Ru and without external promoters. Advanced characterization reveals that the fluorine vacancy formation energies of the alkali and alkaline-earth lattices, together with the vacancy-reactant interactions, dictate the divergent catalytic mechanisms mediated by different active sites. This work expands the chemistry of metal fluorides, launching a new paradigm for potentially viable NH3-synthesis under mild conditions.

item.title: JACS: Hydrogenation of CO2 to Propane and n -Butane by Engineering Metal Oxide Interfacial Structure and Manipulating Zeolite Pore Structure and Acidity
item.description:
Yingnuo Fan, Qian Zhang, Pengcheng Feng, Shiying Li, Sen Wang, Mei Dong, Jianguo Wang, Peng He, et al.
Selective hydrogenation of CO2 to propane and n-butane is of great interest, as these two compounds are not only primary components of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) but also crucial raw materials for preparing propene and a degradable plastic precursor of succinic acid. Although various composite catalysts combining metal oxides and zeolites have been explored, their catalytic performances remain insufficient. Here, we found that ZnZrOx decorated with ultrasmall FeOx clusters, forming an intimate FeOx–ZnZrOx interfacial structure, showed high catalytic activity for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol due to a strong CO2 adsorption capacity and H2 dissociation ability, and silicoaluminophosphate molecular sieve with RHO topological structure enhanced methanol conversion into propane and n-butane via hexamethylbenzenes as active hydrocarbon pool species owing to its unique supercage structure and double eight-membered ring pore opening. As a result, coupling of these two materials delivers a CO2 conversion of ∼66% and a (propane + n-butane) selectivity of 82% in hydrocarbons, which leads to a (propane + n-butane) yield of ∼42%. It is surprising that this composite preferentially produces n-butane rather than iso-butane, and the n-butane/iso-butane ratio is higher than 85.8. The high catalytic stability of this composite is demonstrated by maintaining CO2 conversion, (propane + n-butane) selectivity in hydrocarbons, and their yield of ∼ 61%, ∼ 77%, and ∼ 31%, respectively, after a reaction of 620 h. This work not only fabricates a high-performance catalyst for CO2 hydrogenation to propane and n-butane by engineering the metal oxide interfacial structure and manipulating the zeolite’s pore structure and acidity, but also makes it possible to develop an efficient way for preparing propene and succinic acid from CO2 hydrogenation.

item.title: JACS: Circular RNA Delivery In Vitro and In Vivo Using Doubly Branched Aminoethoxy-Functionalized Ionizable Lipid Nanoparticles
item.description:
Adam Cook, Pavan K. Yadav, Ekram W. Helmy, Kseniia Vlasova, Howard Y. Chang, Paul A. Wender
Circular RNA is a therapeutically promising RNA modality with superior stability and extended protein expression relative to linear RNA. While delivery systems for linear RNA have received much attention, less effort has been directed toward the delivery of circular RNA, whose closed topology and physicochemical properties differ from those of linear RNAs. Here, we disclose a class of ionizable lipids that enable efficient in vitro and in vivo delivery of circular RNA. These ionizable lipids are step-economically accessible, allowing facile assessment of their structure–delivery relationships. Our studies reveal key elements that enhance circular RNA delivery in vitro and in vivo, including aminoethoxy head units, doubly branched tails and linkers tuned for hydrogen bonding and biodegradability. The lead ionizable lipid for circular RNA delivery, iL-19, incorporating these features, achieves ∼28-fold higher protein expression in C2C12 myocytes than Moderna’s SM-102 formulation and 2.5-fold higher expression upon intramuscular administration in BALB/c mice. iL-19 also surpasses benchmark ionizable lipids ALC-0315 (7.8-fold) and DLin-MC3-DMA (33.4-fold) for intramuscular circular RNA delivery in vivo under otherwise identical conditions. This study establishes design principles and a step-economical synthesis for accessing ionizable lipids that enable highly efficient in vitro and in vivo circular RNA delivery.

item.title: JACS: Selective Consecutive Decarboxylation Enables Skeletal Contraction of Waste PET
item.description:
Yue Zhu, Zhouying Mao, Buxing Han, Qingqing Mei
Direct catalytic upcycling of waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) to benzene through consecutive decarboxylation contracts the terephthalate-derived C8 framework to C6, representing a skeletal-editing strategy for aromatic polycarboxylates. The key challenge is to control pathway selection across consecutive decarboxylation steps, favoring sequential aryl–carboxyl C–C bond cleavage over competing hydrogenolysis while preserving the aromatic core. Herein, we report an efficient direct catalytic conversion of waste PET to benzene, achieving an exceptionally high yield of 83.3% over a tailored Ru/W0.4ZrOx catalyst. The performance arises from synergistic acid-site reconstruction and oxygen-vacancy engineering. Moderate WOx incorporation into ZrO2 converts Lewis acidity into Brønsted acidity, while oxygen vacancies and WOx species promote adsorption and activation of carboxyl groups. In cooperation with Ru nanoparticles, these features preferentially stabilize the decarboxylation intermediate over its hydrogenolysis counterpart, directing both consecutive steps toward C–C bond cleavage while suppressing undesired hydrogenolysis pathways. Controlled hydrogen supply and a deliberately designed dodecane/water mixed solvent system further enhance selectivity. The catalyst performs effectively across diverse real-world PET wastes, with preliminary techno-economic and life-cycle analyses indicating favorable process-level metrics under the evaluated assumptions. More broadly, these mechanistic insights establish synergistic acidity and oxygen-vacancy regulation as a catalyst-design principle for decarboxylative skeletal editing of aromatic polycarboxylates.

item.title: JACS: Deciphering Interheme Electron-Transfer Pathways in a Diheme Peroxidase from Methane-Oxidizing Bacteria
item.description:
Riley E. Stein, Anastasia C. Manesis
Bis-FeIV-forming enzymes represent an emerging paradigm in high-valent heme iron chemistry, in which two hemes separated by 15–20 Å are both oxidized to the FeIV state. A tryptophan positioned between the two hemes in two out of the three known enzymes to form this state, MauG and MbnH, has been proposed as the dominant pathway for interheme electron transfer. .The third enzyme, BthA, instead has a serine at this position. Here, we used site-directed mutagenesis of Trp113 in MbnH to test whether this tryptophan is uniquely required for interheme electron transfer. Computational pathway analysis identified the possibility of an alternative, noncovalent route mediated by Arg283 and a heme propionate with possible electronic coupling comparable to that of the native tryptophan pathway. Consistent with this prediction, only simultaneous disruption of both the tryptophan and propionate-mediated pathways abolished bis-FeIV formation entirely. Moreover, only mutants capable of forming bis-FeIV retained the ability to turnover substrate, directly establishing this high-valent state as the catalytic intermediate responsible for substrate modification. These results demonstrate that an intervening tryptophan is not required for fast interheme electron transfer, and instead reveal an additional, noncovalent pathway that may be a general feature of diheme peroxidases.

item.title: JACS: Cesium-Induced Stabilization of the FeOOH Cocatalyst on Bismuth Vanadate Photoanode for Ultraefficient and Stable Photoelectrochemical Water Oxidation
item.description:
Wenchao Jiang, Yange Ma, Ying Tao, Haochuan Jing, Jiazang Chen, Rengui Li, Yi Jiang, Bin Liu
Developing active and durable water oxidation cocatalysts is essential for advancing photoelectrochemical (PEC) water-splitting systems. This study investigates the cesium-induced reconstruction of the FeOOH cocatalyst on a bismuth vanadate (BVO) photoanode for the water oxidation reaction, with a focus on the reconstruction process and its effect in improving interfacial charge transfer and photostability. Cesium ions induce the reconstruction of Fe species on the BVO/FeOOH photoanode during the PEC process, leading to the formation of a robust Cs-incorporated FeOOH (Cs:FeOOH) catalytic layer. Spectroscopic analysis combined with open-circuit potential measurement reveals that the in situ formed Cs:FeOOH cocatalyst can effectively protect BVO and promote interfacial hole transfer during PEC operation. As a result, the BVO/Cs:FeOOH photoanode achieves a photocurrent density of 6.29 mA cm–2 at 1.23 V vs. RHE and maintains stable operation for over 100 h. Furthermore, the Cs-incorporated FeOOH cocatalyst strategy can be extended to other semiconductor systems, including TiO2 and FeOx, highlighting its broader potential for improving solar-driven PEC water oxidation.

item.title: JACS: Electroanalytical and Computational Investigation of Oxoammonium-Mediated Hydride Transfer
item.description:
Elya Kandahari, Natalie A. Cox, Yi Wang, Song Lin
Oxoammonium-mediated hydride transfer is an important yet relatively underexplored elementary step in C–H functionalization. In this work, we employed cyclic voltammetry (CV) to measure the rates of hydride transfer between electrochemically generated oxoammonium catalysts and 42 substrates including ethers, carbamates, amides, and sulfonamides. Through quantum mechanical (QM) calculations, we uncovered a new transition-state model for hydride transfer in which the N atom of the catalyst resides near a heteroatom (X = N or O) of the substrate to allow alignment of the oxoammonium’s O═N+ motif and the substrate’s forming C═X+ bond. Energy decomposition analysis was subsequently performed to elucidate the key factors that govern the kinetics of oxoammonium-mediated hydride transfer. Beyond conventional electronic and steric considerations, we identified substrate distortion, secondary orbital interactions, and noncovalent interactions as critical factors that influence hydride transfer reactivity. We anticipate that these kinetic data along with the mechanistic insights they provide will inform future catalyst development and synthetic applications to broaden the scope of oxoammonium catalysis.

item.title: JACS: Birch-Type-Reduced Carbazole Anions Enable Redox-Adaptive Super-Reducing Photocatalysis
item.description:
Yi-Ming Chen, Yu Liu, Zhi-Ao Tian, Ming-Xuan Gao, Hao-Zhe Dong, Bai-Yi Zhang, Xiao-Ning Guo, Hong Yi, et al.
Photocatalytic activation of inert chemical bonds is constrained by the redox potential of the catalyst. Here, we report a redox-adaptive photocatalytic strategy in which an electron-rich carbazole photocatalyst, CBZ6, functions as a molecular redox transformer through the formation of Birch-type carbazole anions. Under visible light, CBZ6 switches between a neutral state for conventional photoredox reactions and an anionic state for super-reducing catalysis. Excitation of the anionic state generates a super-reducing species with an excited-state oxidation potential of approximately −3.6 V versus SCE, substantially beyond that of the neutral excited state (−2.2 V). This adaptive redox switching enables activation of otherwise inaccessible C–F bonds in aryl fluorides, polyfluoroalkyl compounds, and fluoropolymers. The complementary reactivities of the two states further enable diverse photoredox transformations, establishing redox adaptation as a strategy for expanding the accessible reactivity of organic photocatalysts.

item.title: JACS: Regio- and Enantioselective Functionalization of Gaseous Alkanes via Nickel-Catalyzed Alkene Dicarbofunctionalization
item.description:
